In-scope processes.value: Statutory close for every licensed carrier: trial-balance close, statutory-basis adjustments, reserve and asset valuation load, Japan FSA business report (gyomu hokokusho) per Art. 110, and the NAIC Annual and Quarterly Statement blanks for each US writing company

In-scope systems.value: Statutory blanks software fed from the ERP general ledger and the valuation system; Japan business report forms assembled from the same closed trial balance

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Financial Statement Preparation Procedure - close calendar, statutory-basis adjustment inventory (non-admitted assets, deferred tax admissibility, reserve postings), blanks page ownership map, cross-check and jurat sign-off

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and reviewed by the Audit Committee annually, plus on any NAIC Annual Statement Instructions change or FSA ordinance amendment to the Art. 110 forms

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Japan: business report and financial statements to the FSA within three months of the 31 March business year end (30 June), interim report for the half-year; US: Annual Statement 1 March, quarterly statements 15 May / 15 August / 15 November

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close-calendar tasks with alerts at day-20, day-10 and day-3 before each statutory due date, one task per blanks page owner and one per Japan form; unclosed tasks escalate daily to the Controller

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed jurat pages, filed PDF of the Art. 110 business report with the FSA receipt, trial balance to blanks tie-out, statutory adjustment workpapers and reserve certificates retained 10 years from the business year end

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any late statement, refiled amended blank, or cross-check that stayed unresolved at filing is logged with the page, the amount, the cause and the amended-filing date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off every amended statement and every statutory-basis adjustment change made after the first submission

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every statutory statement filed for the year by every licensed entity: the Japan Art. 110 business report and financial statements, and each US company's Annual Statement and three quarterly statements

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero unexplained differences between the closed trial balance and the filed statements above 0.5 percent of surplus or JPY 100 million, zero unresolved NAIC cross-checks at filing, zero statements filed after the statutory due date

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with quarterly interim statements; test runs after each filing, with the full re-performance test after the annual statement and a reduced tie-out test each quarter

checklist.step: Publish the statutory close calendar and the page ownership map
actions: Build the close calendar backwards from the two hard dates: the Japan Art. 110 business report at three months after the 31 March business year end, and the NAIC Annual Statement on 1 March.

Create one task per statement page and per Japan form, naming an owner from Financial Reporting, Investment Accounting, Reinsurance Accounting, Actuarial and Tax, with a preparer and a reviewer on each.
Set the freeze date for the general ledger and circulate it to the Controller, the Appointed Actuary and the Investment Operations Manager so late journals stop arriving after the tie-out.
Publish the calendar in the close tool and confirm every task has an accepted owner before the close opens.
checklist.done: every blanks page and Japan form has a named preparer, reviewer and due date inside the close calendar, and the ledger freeze date is circulated.

checklist.step: Close the general ledger and lock the statutory trial balance
actions: Run the period-end close in the general ledger for each legal entity, post accruals for premium, commission, reinsurance and expense cut-off, and close the sub-ledgers in order: billing, claims, investment accounting, then general ledger.
Export the trial balance by legal entity and statutory account, and confirm debits equal credits and the entity roll-up ties to the consolidation.
Set the ledger period to closed and grant post-close journal rights only to the Controller, logging each post-close entry with a reason on the close checklist.
Hand the locked trial balance file, stamped with entity, period and export timestamp, to the Statutory Reporting Manager as the single source for every page.
checklist.done: the ledger is closed, balanced by entity, and one timestamped trial balance is released as the sole feed for statutory reporting.

checklist.step: Apply the statutory-basis adjustments off the closed GAAP ledger
actions: Work the statutory adjustment inventory line by line: non-admit furniture, equipment, prepaid expenses, agents balances over 90 days past due and disallowed deferred tax assets under the admissibility test.
Reverse GAAP deferred acquisition costs and record acquisition costs as expensed in the period, per the statutory basis.
For the Japan entity, book the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve accrual, the Art. 116 policy reserve and the Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve postings supplied by the Appointed Actuary.
Record each adjustment as a numbered journal with a support reference, and reconcile the adjusted statutory surplus to prior-period surplus in a roll-forward.
Send the adjustment schedule to the Controller for review before any page is populated.
checklist.done: every statutory adjustment is a numbered, supported journal and the surplus roll-forward from prior period to current period is explained in full.

checklist.step: Load reserves and the actuarial exhibits from the valuation system
actions: Run the year-end valuation on the frozen in-force extract and produce the aggregate reserve for life contracts, deposit-type contract liabilities and the claim reserve by line of business.
Tie the valuation output to the reserve balances posted in the ledger and clear any difference with Financial Reporting before the exhibits are cut.

Populate Exhibit 5 (aggregate reserve for life contracts), Exhibit 7 (deposit-type contracts) and Exhibit 8 (claim reserves), and the Japan policy reserve and outstanding claims tables required by Art. 116 and Art. 117.
Hand the Appointed Actuary the reserve summary, the valuation basis table and the asset adequacy testing results that support the opinion.
checklist.done: reserve exhibits are populated from the valuation run, agree to the ledger balances, and the Appointed Actuary holds the supporting valuation basis and asset adequacy results.

checklist.step: Build the investment schedules from the custodian and investment accounting records
actions: Reconcile the investment accounting position file to the custodian statement at CUSIP or ISIN level for units, book value, amortised cost and market value, and clear breaks before the schedules are cut.

Populate Schedule D Part 1 (bonds), Part 2 (preferred and common stock), Part 3 (acquisitions) and Part 4 (disposals), Schedule BA, Schedule DA and Schedule DB, and confirm each carries the NAIC designation from the SVO or the filing-exempt rating.

For the Japan entity produce the securities holdings and valuation tables that support the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve base, split by domestic stock, bond, foreign-currency asset and real estate.
Send the schedule totals to Financial Reporting and confirm they tie to the invested asset lines on the balance sheet page.
checklist.done: investment schedules reconcile to the custodian at security level and the schedule totals agree to the balance sheet invested asset lines.

checklist.step: Reconcile reinsurance balances and populate the reinsurance schedules
actions: Extract ceded premium, ceded losses, funds withheld and reinsurance recoverable by reinsurer and treaty from the ceded accounting platform for the statement period.
Confirm each reinsurer NAIC company code, FEIN and authorised/unauthorised status, and compute the provision for reinsurance for unauthorised and slow-paying balances.
Populate the reinsurance schedules and the ceded columns of the underwriting exhibit, and agree reinsurance recoverable to the reinsurer confirmations returned for the year.
Report any reinsurer with an unconfirmed balance above the materiality threshold to the Controller for a written explanation before filing.
checklist.done: ceded balances agree to the ledger and the reinsurer confirmations, and every unauthorised balance carries a computed provision.

checklist.step: Populate the core financial pages and the Japan Art. 110 forms
actions: Import the locked trial balance into the statutory blanks software with the mapping table from statutory account to page and line, and review every unmapped account rather than defaulting it.
Populate Assets, Liabilities Surplus and Other Funds, the Summary of Operations, the Cash Flow statement and the Analysis of Operations by line of business.

Assemble the Japan business report in the prescribed Cabinet Office Ordinance form set: balance sheet, profit and loss statement, statement of changes in net assets, and the business overview sections required by Art. 110.
Run the software import log and clear every warning; do not overwrite an imported figure by hand without a documented override note.
checklist.done: all core pages and the Japan Art. 110 form set are populated from the mapped trial balance with a clean import log and every override documented.

checklist.step: Tie the filed pages back to the trial balance line by line
actions: Build the tie-out workbook with one row per statement line, showing the trial balance amount, the statutory adjustment, the page amount and the difference.
Investigate every non-zero difference and write the explanation and the supporting journal reference on the row - a blank explanation is not a completed tie-out.
Foot and cross-foot total assets, total liabilities and surplus, and confirm total assets equal total liabilities plus surplus on the filed page.
Have the Controller initial the tie-out workbook before the cross-checks are run.
checklist.done: every statement line ties to the trial balance plus a referenced adjustment, and the balance sheet foots and cross-foots on the filed page.

checklist.step: Run and clear the NAIC cross-checks and validation edits
actions: Run the full cross-check and validation edit routine in the blanks software for the statement type and year.
Work each failed check to a resolution: correct the underlying figure where the check is right, or write a cross-check explanation where the difference is legitimate and permitted.
Re-run the routine until the only remaining items are explained checks, and export the final edit report into the close file.
Escalate any check that cannot be corrected before the due date to the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Controller with the amount and the affected page.
checklist.done: the validation run is clean or every remaining check carries a written explanation, and the final edit report is filed in the close file.

checklist.step: Draft the Notes to Financial Statements and the narrative disclosures
actions: Roll forward each note from prior year and update the figures from the current tie-out: accounting practices and permitted practices, investments, reinsurance, related party transactions, contingencies and subsequent events.
Collect the related party balances from the holding company reporting pack and the litigation and contingency inputs from Legal Counsel in writing.
For the Japan business report write the business overview narrative sections including the solvency margin ratio disclosure and the reserve accumulation commentary.
Circulate the note draft to the Controller, the Appointed Actuary and General Counsel and record their comments and clearances in the repository.
checklist.done: all notes and narrative sections are updated to current-year figures with written inputs from Legal and Actuarial and recorded clearances.

checklist.step: Obtain the actuarial opinion and the officer certifications
actions: Review the completed reserve exhibits against the valuation results and the asset adequacy analysis for the business year.
Issue the Statement of Actuarial Opinion covering the reserve items, naming the scope, the reliance on data supplied by Financial Reporting, and any qualification.
Provide the supporting actuarial memorandum and the regulatory asset adequacy issues summary to the Controller for the file.
Confirm the opinion date is on or before the statement filing date and that the reserve amounts in the opinion match the filed exhibits to the yen and dollar.
checklist.done: a signed actuarial opinion dated on or before the filing date exists and its reserve amounts match the filed exhibits exactly.

checklist.step: Review the complete statement package before sign-off
actions: Read the assembled package end to end against the review checklist: page completeness, prior-year comparatives, signature blocks, and the surplus roll-forward explanation.
Compare every major line to prior period and to plan, and require a written explanation from the page owner for any movement above the review threshold.
Confirm the statutory adjustment inventory, the tie-out workbook, the cleared edit report and the actuarial opinion are all present in the close file.
Record the review as complete in the close tool and release the package for officer signature.
checklist.done: the Controller has signed off a complete package with every threshold-breaching movement explained in writing.

checklist.step: Execute the jurat and the officer signatures
actions: Confirm the jurat page carries the correct company name, NAIC company code, FEIN, statutory home office address and the officer and director names for the statement year.
Have the officers required by the blank sign the jurat, and obtain the notarisation or the electronic equivalent the state accepts.
For the Japan business report obtain the representative director signature or seal on the submission cover form required by the Cabinet Office Ordinance.
File the executed signature pages into the close file and link them to the statement version being filed - never to a superseded draft.
checklist.done: executed jurat and Japan cover-form signatures exist, match the exact statement version being filed, and are stored in the close file.

checklist.step: Hand the signed statements to Regulatory Reporting for submission
actions: Generate the final filing files from the blanks software: the electronic filing file, the PDF of the printed statement, and the supporting schedule attachments.
Log the package into the regulatory filing record with entity, statement type, statement period, due date and the target regulators.
Notify the Regulatory Reporting Analyst that the package is released, and confirm the Japan form set is released to the officer responsible for the FSA electronic submission.
Freeze the statement version so no further edit is possible without a version increment and a documented reason.
checklist.done: a frozen, versioned filing package is released to Regulatory Reporting with the due dates and target regulators recorded.

checklist.step: Archive the statement evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the close file into the evidence repository under entity and business year: trial balance, adjustment journals, tie-out workbook, edit report, notes support, actuarial opinion, signed jurat, filed statement PDF and the FSA receipt.
Apply the 10-year-from-business-year-end retention label so the record survives an FSA inspection cycle and a state examination cycle.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by entity, business year, statement type and NAIC company code.
Record the archive completion date on the close calendar and close the period tasks.
checklist.done: the full close file is archived under entity and business year, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by company code.

testing.step: Build the population of statutory statements filed for the year
actions: Extract from the regulatory filing record every statutory statement filed in the period by entity: the Japan Art. 110 business report and financial statements, and each US company Annual and quarterly statement.
Cross-check the extract against the list of licensed entities held by the Corporate Secretary so no licensed carrier is missing from the population.
Add any amended or refiled statement as its own population row so restatements cannot be tested away.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete with the extract date and record count.
testing.done: the population lists every statement for every licensed entity, includes amendments, and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed statements back to the locked trial balance
actions: Pull the timestamped trial balance released for the statement period and independently re-map it to statement pages using the approved mapping table.
Compare independently derived total assets, total liabilities, surplus and net income to the filed figures for each entity.
Investigate every difference above 0.5 percent of surplus or JPY 100 million and trace it to a numbered statutory adjustment journal.
Treat any difference with no supporting journal as an automatic exception, not a mapping preference.
testing.done: filed totals reconcile to the independently re-mapped trial balance with every material difference traced to a numbered journal.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of statement pages and adjustments
actions: Take 100 percent of the Japan Art. 110 forms and 100 percent of the annual balance sheet, summary of operations and reserve exhibit pages.
Take 25 statutory adjustment journals selected at random with a recorded seed, plus every adjustment above the surplus materiality threshold.
Record the population size, the seed, the selection date and the selector in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Confirm the sample spans every legal entity and both the annual and quarterly statement types.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all key pages, every material adjustment and every legal entity is documented in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the statutory-basis adjustments on the sample
actions: Recompute each sampled non-admitted asset independently: agents balances aged over 90 days from the receivable ageing, prepaid and furniture balances from the fixed asset register, and the deferred tax admissibility calculation.
Recompute the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve accrual for the Japan entity from the asset class balances and the ordinance rate applicable to each class.
Compare each recomputed figure to the posted journal and record the difference in the workpaper with the direction of the error.
Escalate any adjustment that overstates surplus to the Chief Financial Officer the same day it is found.
testing.done: each sampled adjustment is independently recomputed and any surplus-overstating difference is escalated the day it is identified.

testing.step: Re-perform the reserve exhibit tie to the valuation output
actions: Obtain the valuation run output used for the statement period directly from the actuarial platform rather than from the reporting pack.
Agree the aggregate reserve, deposit-type liabilities and claim reserve by line of business to the filed reserve exhibits and to the ledger reserve balances.
Confirm the in-force extract date used by the valuation matches the statement period end and that the run was not re-executed after the ledger freeze.
Confirm the signed actuarial opinion quotes the same reserve amounts as the filed exhibits.
testing.done: reserve exhibits, ledger balances, valuation output and the actuarial opinion all carry identical reserve amounts for the period.

testing.step: Verify investment schedules against the custodian record
actions: Select 40 securities across Schedule D Part 1 and Part 2 and the Japan securities valuation table, weighted to the largest holdings.
Agree units, book or amortised value, market value and acquisition date to the custodian statement at CUSIP or ISIN level.
Confirm the NAIC designation on each sampled bond against the SVO listing or the filing-exempt rating in force at period end.
Recompute the schedule totals and agree them to the invested asset lines on the filed balance sheet.
testing.done: sampled securities agree to the custodian at security level, designations are supported, and schedule totals agree to the balance sheet.

testing.step: Re-run the validation edits on the filed statement version
actions: Open the exact frozen statement version that was filed and re-run the full cross-check and validation edit routine.
Compare the re-run edit report to the report kept in the close file and investigate any check that appears in one and not the other.
Read each retained cross-check explanation and judge whether it explains the difference or merely restates it.
Record any check that was open and unexplained at filing as an exception with the page, line and amount.
testing.done: the re-run edit report matches the filed close-file report and every retained explanation is judged adequate or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the filing deadline maths and prove timeliness
actions: For the Japan entity, compute the Art. 110 due date as three months from the 31 March business year end and compare it to the FSA submission receipt timestamp.
For each US entity, compare the submission timestamp to the 1 March annual and 15 May, 15 August and 15 November quarterly due dates.
Where the statement was filed on the due date, confirm the receipt or confirmation carries a timestamp before the regulator cut-off rather than an internal send time.
Log any statement filed late with the number of days late and the reason recorded by the Controller.
testing.done: every statement has a regulator-side receipt timestamp compared against the recomputed due date, with days late quantified where applicable.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the entity, statement type, page and line, the amount and the surplus effect.
Assign a root cause from the standard set: mapping error, unposted adjustment, valuation-to-ledger break, custodian break, missed deadline, or unsupported override.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and where the exception changes filed figures, open an amended-statement decision with the Controller and General Counsel.
Carry every open exception forward as a mandatory retest row in the next quarter's statement test.
testing.done: every exception has a tracked issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and an amended-filing decision where figures change.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the statement verification
actions: Compute the exception rate against the sample and compare the material-difference total to the zero-tolerance and 0.5-percent-of-surplus thresholds.
Write the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper references behind each judgement.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and reviewed none of the statement pages, sign the workpaper and date the sign-off.
Report the conclusion and any amended-filing decisions to the Audit Committee at its next meeting and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Build the regulator matrix for the statement period
actions: List every licensed entity from the Corporate Secretary licence register and, for each, every jurisdiction where it holds a certificate of authority or an FSA licence.
For each entity and jurisdiction record the filing type due, the channel (NAIC electronic filing, state portal, FSA electronic notification, or paper), the due date and any filing fee.
Mark the domiciliary regulator separately, since it receives the full statement plus the supplemental and RBC filings.
Publish the matrix as the single filing checklist for the period and route it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for approval.
checklist.done: an approved matrix exists with one row per entity, per jurisdiction, per filing type, showing channel, due date and fee.

checklist.step: Compute and review the price fluctuation reserve balance
actions: Pull the period-end asset balances by class from investment accounting: domestic stocks, domestic bonds, foreign-currency denominated assets, and real estate.
Apply the accumulation rate prescribed for each class by the Ordinance for Enforcement of the Insurance Business Act to compute the required annual Art. 115 accrual.
Compare the accumulated balance to the prescribed ceiling for each class and cap the accrual where the ceiling is reached, documenting the cap on the calculation sheet.
Send the calculation with the asset balances and rates applied to the Controller for review and posting.
checklist.done: the Art. 115 accrual is computed by asset class at the ordinance rate, capped at the prescribed ceiling, and reviewed by the Controller.

checklist.step: Gate any price fluctuation reserve drawdown against the statutory threshold
actions: Where a drawdown is proposed, quantify the realized losses on price-variable assets for the business year from the investment accounting disposal records.
Compare those realized losses to the prescribed threshold above which Art. 115 permits a drawdown, and compute the maximum permitted drawdown amount.
Write a drawdown memo stating the realized loss amount, the threshold test, the permitted amount and the amount actually taken, and route it to the Chief Financial Officer for approval.
Refuse any drawdown proposed to smooth earnings where the realized-loss threshold is not met, and record the refusal.
checklist.done: no drawdown is posted without a memo showing realized losses above the prescribed threshold and a CFO approval.

checklist.step: Confirm the reserve tables agree across the Japan and US statements
actions: Agree the Art. 116 policy reserve and Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve balances in the Japan schedules to the ledger reserve accounts and to the valuation output.
Agree the equivalent reserve lines on the US statement liability page to the same ledger accounts for the corresponding entity.
Document any presentation difference between the two frameworks on a bridging schedule rather than adjusting one to match the other.
Obtain the Appointed Actuary confirmation that both presentations are supported by the same valuation run.
checklist.done: reserve balances in both frameworks trace to the same ledger accounts and valuation run, with presentation differences bridged in writing.

checklist.step: Generate and validate the electronic filing file
actions: In the blanks software select the frozen filed version and generate the electronic filing file for the statement type and year.
Run the pre-submission validation and confirm the file header carries the correct NAIC company code, group code, FEIN and statement period.
Confirm the file includes all required supplements and schedules for the period and that no page is flagged as incomplete.
Save the generated file and the validation log to the submission folder named by entity, statement type and period.
checklist.done: a validated electronic filing file with a correct header and no incomplete pages sits in the submission folder.

checklist.step: Upload the statement to the NAIC Financial Data Repository
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ with the company filer credentials and open the Financial Data Repository upload function for the statement year.
Select the entity by NAIC company code, choose the statement type and period, and attach the generated electronic filing file and the signed PDF.
Submit and wait for the acceptance response rather than closing the session on the upload acknowledgement.
Capture the confirmation screen showing the accepted file name, company code, statement period and the submission timestamp, and save it to the submission folder.
checklist.done: the statement is accepted by the NAIC repository and an accepted-status confirmation with a timestamp is saved for the entity.

checklist.step: File with the domiciliary regulator and each non-domiciliary state
actions: Work the regulator matrix state by state and submit through the channel that state accepts, using the NAIC filing checklist entry for that state as the authority.
For states that require a hard copy or a signed original jurat, courier the package with tracking and record the tracking number on the matrix row.
Pay each filing fee through the method the state accepts and attach the payment confirmation to the matrix row.
Mark each row filed only when the state-side receipt, stamped copy or portal confirmation is in hand.
checklist.done: every matrix row shows a state-side receipt or tracking evidence and, where applicable, a fee payment confirmation.

checklist.step: Submit the Japan reserve schedules through the FSA channel
actions: Assemble the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve schedule, the Art. 116 policy reserve tables and the Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve tables in the prescribed ordinance form set.
Submit them with the Art. 110 business report through the FSA electronic application and notification system under the company filer account.
Download the submission receipt showing the accepted forms, the submitting entity and the receipt date and time.
Notify the Chief Financial Officer and the Appointed Actuary that the FSA submission is receipted.
checklist.done: the FSA submission carries a downloaded receipt naming the accepted reserve forms and its date and time.

checklist.step: File the RBC report and the actuarial opinion with the domiciliary regulator
actions: Generate the risk-based capital report from the filed statement figures and confirm the total adjusted capital and authorised control level amounts recompute from the statement pages.
File the RBC report and the signed Statement of Actuarial Opinion with the domiciliary regulator and the NAIC on the 1 March due date.
Confirm the reported RBC ratio and, where it falls in any action level, notify the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Risk Officer the same day.
Save the RBC filing confirmation alongside the statement receipt in the submission folder.
checklist.done: the RBC report and actuarial opinion are filed by the due date and the resulting ratio is reported to the CFO and CRO.

checklist.step: Capture and index every submission receipt
actions: For each matrix row attach the receipt artefact: NAIC acceptance screen, state portal confirmation, courier proof of delivery, or FSA electronic receipt.
Record the regulator-side timestamp on the row, not the internal send time, and flag any row whose only evidence is an internal email.
Index the receipts by entity, jurisdiction, filing type and period so a single row can be produced on request.
Report any row still without a receipt 3 business days after submission to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: every matrix row carries a regulator-side receipt with its timestamp indexed by entity, jurisdiction, filing type and period.

checklist.step: Work rejections and resubmissions to closure
actions: Monitor the NAIC repository status list and the state portals daily during the filing window for rejected or pending-correction submissions.
For each rejection read the error reason, route the correction to the responsible page owner in Financial Reporting or Actuarial, and set a same-week correction date.
Resubmit the corrected file, capture the new acceptance confirmation, and keep both the rejection and the acceptance in the folder.
Log each rejection in the tracker with the cause so recurring causes can be fixed before the next filing wave.
checklist.done: no submission remains in rejected or pending status, and each rejection carries a logged cause and an acceptance confirmation.

checklist.step: File the supplemental and 1 April filings from the same statement version
actions: Work the supplemental filing list for the statement year and confirm each supplement due 1 April is generated from the same frozen statement version as the annual statement.
Where a supplement does not apply to the entity, file the not-applicable response the instructions require rather than omitting the filing.
Upload each supplement and capture its own acceptance confirmation on its own matrix row.
Reconcile the supplement figures to the annual statement pages they derive from before submission.
checklist.done: every supplement is filed or answered not applicable by 1 April, generated from the frozen statement version, with its own confirmation.

checklist.step: Report filing completion status to Finance leadership
actions: Produce a completion report from the matrix showing filings due, filed on time, filed late, rejected and outstanding, by entity and jurisdiction.
Attach the reserve summary showing the Art. 115 accrual, any drawdown taken and the closing reserve balance.
Send the report to the Chief Financial Officer and the Controller within 5 business days of the filing wave closing.
Present any late or outstanding filing with its cause and the remediation owner named.
checklist.done: a completion report covering every matrix row and the reserve movement is issued to the CFO and Controller within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Refresh the matrix from the reissued NAIC and FSA requirements
actions: Read the reissued NAIC Annual Statement Instructions and filing checklist for the coming statement year and mark every changed state requirement.
Read FSA ordinance amendments affecting the Art. 115 rate table, reserve forms or submission channel and record the effective business year.
Update the regulator matrix rows, channels, fees and due dates and record the source document and date on each changed row.
Brief the Regulatory Reporting Analyst and the Controller on the changes before the next close opens.
checklist.done: the matrix is updated for the new statement year with a cited source on every changed row and the change is briefed to the close team.

checklist.step: Archive the submission evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the submission folder into the evidence repository under entity and business year: matrix, filing files, acceptance confirmations, state receipts, fee proofs, FSA receipt and the reserve calculation.
Apply the 10-year-from-business-year-end retention label to the whole folder.
Confirm the record is retrievable by NAIC company code, jurisdiction and filing type.
Close the period tasks in the tracker only after the archive is confirmed.
checklist.done: the submission evidence is archived under entity and business year, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by company code and jurisdiction.

testing.step: Build the expected-filings population independently of the matrix
actions: Take the licence register from the Corporate Secretary and the FSA licence record, and derive the list of entities and jurisdictions that owed a filing for the period.
Derive the filing types due for each from the NAIC filing checklist and the Cabinet Office Ordinance form set, without using the regulatory reporting matrix as the source.
Compare the derived list to the matrix and treat any jurisdiction present in the licence register but absent from the matrix as an automatic exception.
Sign the derived population as complete with the extract date and the source registers named.
testing.done: an independently derived expected-filings population exists and every matrix omission is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Reconcile filed submissions to the expected population
actions: Match each expected row to a logged submission on entity, jurisdiction, filing type and period.
List unmatched expected rows as missed filings and unmatched submissions as unplanned filings, and pursue both.
Confirm each match carries a receipt artefact and not just a status flag set by the preparer.
Quantify the count of expected, matched, missed and unplanned rows in the workpaper.
testing.done: every expected filing is matched to a receipted submission or listed as a missed filing with a count in the workpaper.

testing.step: Draw and document the receipt sample
actions: Take 100 percent of domiciliary regulator filings, 100 percent of the FSA submissions and 100 percent of the RBC and actuarial opinion filings.
Take 30 non-domiciliary state rows at random with a recorded seed across all entities and both annual and quarterly waves.
Record the population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every row that was rejected or resubmitted during the period as a mandatory sample item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all domiciliary, FSA, RBC and rejected rows plus 30 random state rows is documented.

testing.step: Verify each sampled receipt inside the regulator system
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ and open the Financial Data Repository filing status list for the entity and statement year.
Confirm the sampled filing shows accepted status with the correct company code, statement type and period, and read the regulator-side timestamp.
For state and FSA rows, open the portal record or the electronic receipt and confirm the same details rather than relying on the stored screenshot alone.
Treat any row where the regulator system shows no record, or a different period, as an exception regardless of the stored evidence.
testing.done: each sampled filing is confirmed as accepted inside the regulator system itself with a matching entity, type and period.

testing.step: Recompute the due dates and measure timeliness
actions: Recompute each due date from the statute and instructions: 1 March annual, 15 May, 15 August and 15 November quarterly, 1 April supplements, and three months from 31 March for the FSA report.
Compare each recomputed due date to the regulator-side timestamp and compute days early or days late for every sampled row.
Check that a due date falling on a weekend or holiday was rolled the way the instructions require, not the way the preparer assumed.
List every row filed after the due date with the days late and the entity, and treat it as a fail regardless of cause.
testing.done: days early or late is computed for every sampled row from an independently recomputed due date, with late rows listed as fails.

testing.step: Re-perform the price fluctuation reserve calculation
actions: Pull the period-end asset balances by class directly from investment accounting rather than from the preparer sheet.
Apply the ordinance accumulation rate for each class independently and compute the required accrual and the prescribed ceiling.
Compare the recomputed accrual and closing balance to the posted and filed amounts and quantify any difference.
Confirm the asset classification used matches the classification in the investment schedules filed with the statement.
testing.done: the Art. 115 accrual, ceiling and closing balance are independently recomputed and any difference to the filed amount is quantified.

testing.step: Test every reserve drawdown against the Art. 115 threshold
actions: Identify every debit to the price fluctuation reserve in the period from the ledger account activity, not from the drawdown memo list.
For each debit, obtain the realized loss evidence from the investment disposal records and test it against the prescribed threshold for permitted drawdown.
Confirm the drawdown amount does not exceed the permitted maximum and that a dated Chief Financial Officer approval pre-dates the posting.
Treat any debit without realized losses above the threshold as a reportable breach of Art. 115, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every reserve debit is traced to realized losses above the statutory threshold with a pre-dated CFO approval, or reported as a breach.

testing.step: Trace rejections and resubmissions to a clean final state
actions: Extract every rejection and pending-correction event logged during the filing waves.
For each, confirm the corrected file was resubmitted, accepted, and that the accepted version matches the frozen statement version signed on the jurat.
Check whether the resubmission cleared before or after the statutory due date and count the late ones.
Group rejections by cause and flag any cause that recurred across more than one filing wave.
testing.done: every rejection ends in an accepted resubmission tied to the signed statement version, with late clears counted and recurring causes flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the entity, jurisdiction, filing type, the due date, the actual receipt date and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the standard set: matrix omission, channel error, fee failure, upload rejection, late close, or unsupported reserve drawdown.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and open a self-report assessment with General Counsel for any missed statutory filing or Art. 115 breach.
Carry every open exception into the next filing wave as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has a tracked issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where statutory, a self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the submission test
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate and the receipt-evidence rate and compare both to the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper reference for each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither prepared nor uploaded any sampled submission, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, late filings and any Art. 115 breach to the Audit Committee at its next meeting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating the on-time rate, the conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Inventory every schedule and exhibit the entity owes this year
actions: Read the schedule and supplemental filing list in the Annual Statement Instructions for the statement year and the blank type the entity files.
Build an inventory row per schedule and exhibit with the owner, the source system extract, the due date and whether it is applicable to the entity.
Add the Japan annex forms required with the Art. 110 report: asset valuation tables, the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve schedule, and the Art. 116 and Art. 117 reserve tables.
Route the inventory to the Controller for approval so no schedule reaches the filing date without a named owner.
checklist.done: an approved inventory names an owner, a source extract and a due date for every schedule, exhibit and Japan annex form.

checklist.step: Freeze the source extracts that feed the schedules
actions: Run the period-end extracts after the ledger freeze: investment position and transaction files, ceded reinsurance balances, premium by state, and policy counts by line.
Stamp each extract with the source system, the as-of date, the run timestamp and the record count, and store it read-only.
Reconcile each extract control total back to the ledger account it supports and report any break to the schedule owner before work starts.
Publish the extract list so every schedule owner uses the same frozen file rather than a private query.
checklist.done: one stamped, read-only extract per source exists, control totals tie to the ledger, and every schedule owner is pointed at it.

checklist.step: Build the bond and stock schedules with designations
actions: Populate Schedule D Part 1 for bonds with CUSIP or ISIN, description, acquisition date, par value, book or adjusted carrying value, fair value, effective rate and the NAIC designation.
Populate Schedule D Part 2 for preferred and common stock with the same identifiers plus dividends received during the year.
Assign the NAIC designation from the SVO listing, or the filing-exempt mapping from the credit rating in force at period end, and record which basis was used per security.
Reconcile the schedule totals to the invested asset lines on the balance sheet page and clear any difference with Financial Reporting.
checklist.done: bond and stock schedules carry an identifier, valuation, designation and designation basis per security, and total to the balance sheet lines.

checklist.step: Build the acquisition, disposal and short-term schedules
actions: Populate Schedule D Part 3 for securities acquired during the year with acquisition date, cost, and the name of the vendor or exchange.
Populate Schedule D Part 4 for securities disposed with disposal date, consideration received, book value at disposal and the realized gain or loss.
Populate Schedule DA for short-term investments and Schedule DB for derivatives with the counterparty, notional, fair value and the hedge designation.
Confirm the realized gains and losses in Part 4 total to the realized gain line in the summary of operations, and use the same disposal file that supports the Art. 115 drawdown test.
checklist.done: acquisitions, disposals, short-term and derivative schedules are complete and realized gains and losses tie to the summary of operations.

checklist.step: Build the real estate, mortgage and other invested asset schedules
actions: Populate Schedule A for real estate with property location, acquisition date, cost, accumulated depreciation and current book value from the fixed asset register.
Populate Schedule B for mortgage loans with loan number, property type, interest rate, outstanding balance and the arrears status.
Populate Schedule BA for other long-term invested assets including limited partnership and joint venture interests, with the valuation method used for each.
Reconcile each schedule to its ledger account balance and provide the class totals to the Art. 115 reserve calculation owner.
checklist.done: real estate, mortgage and other invested asset schedules reconcile to their ledger accounts and their class totals are handed to the reserve calculation.

checklist.step: Build the Japan asset valuation annex and the price fluctuation reserve schedule
actions: Split the period-end asset base into the classes the ordinance uses for Art. 115: domestic stocks, domestic bonds, foreign-currency denominated assets and real estate.
For each class show book value, market value, unrealized gain or loss, the ordinance accumulation rate applied, the required accrual and the prescribed ceiling.
Show the opening reserve balance, the accrual, any drawdown with its realized-loss support, and the closing balance for the business year.
Cross-check the class book values to the corresponding US schedule totals and explain any difference from valuation-basis differences on the face of the annex.
checklist.done: the Art. 115 annex shows the reserve roll-forward by asset class with rates, ceilings and a cross-check to the US schedule totals.

checklist.step: Build the reinsurance schedules and the recoverable ageing
actions: List each reinsurer with NAIC company code, FEIN, domicile and authorised or unauthorised status, and the treaty identifiers ceded to it.
Populate ceded premium, ceded losses paid, ceded reserves, funds held and the reinsurance recoverable, aged by days outstanding.
Compute the provision for reinsurance on unauthorised and slow-paying balances and post it before the liability page is finalised.
Agree the recoverable balances to the reinsurer confirmations returned for the year and escalate any unconfirmed material balance to the Controller.
checklist.done: reinsurance schedules carry authorised status, aged recoverables, a computed provision and confirmation support for material balances.

checklist.step: Build the premiums-by-state and holding company schedules
actions: Extract direct written premium, direct earned premium and direct losses paid by state and by line from policy administration for the statement year.
Confirm the state allocation follows the situs rule the instructions require, and that the state list matches the certificate of authority register held by the Corporate Secretary.
Populate the holding company schedule with every affiliate transaction: management fees, cost sharing, intercompany reinsurance, loans and dividends, with amounts and counterparties.
Agree the premiums-by-state total to the direct premium line in the underwriting exhibit and the affiliate amounts to the related party note.
checklist.done: premiums by state total to the underwriting exhibit, the state list matches the licence register, and affiliate amounts agree to the related party note.

checklist.step: Build the five-year historical page and the comparative exhibits
actions: Pull the four prior years from the previously filed statements rather than from the internal reporting pack, so restated internal figures cannot leak in.
Populate the five-year historical page and confirm each prior-year column matches the statement as originally filed for that year.
Where a prior year was amended, use the amended filed figure and note the amendment on the workpaper.
Explain any current-year movement above the review threshold in the analytical review memo attached to the page.
checklist.done: prior-year columns match the statements as filed, amendments are noted, and threshold-breaching movements are explained in the review memo.

checklist.step: Run the interlock checks between schedules and the financial pages
actions: Run the schedule-to-page interlock checks in the blanks software: asset schedule totals to the asset page, reinsurance schedule totals to the ceded columns, premiums by state to the underwriting exhibit.
Work every failed interlock back to the source extract and correct the schedule, not the page, unless the page is demonstrably wrong.
Where the instructions permit a difference, record the permitted explanation and the amount on the interlock log.
Re-run the checks until the log holds only explained items and export the final log to the close file.
checklist.done: every schedule-to-page interlock passes or carries a permitted, quantified explanation on the exported interlock log.

checklist.step: File a not-applicable response for every schedule the entity does not owe
actions: Work the inventory rows marked not applicable and confirm the instructions permit a not-applicable response rather than omission.
Enter the response the instructions prescribe - a none page, a zero schedule or a written statement - for each such row.
Record on the inventory why the schedule does not apply, naming the business the entity does not write or the asset class it does not hold.
Have the Controller review the not-applicable list before filing so no schedule is dropped by assumption.
checklist.done: every not-applicable schedule carries the prescribed response and a Controller-reviewed reason on the inventory.

checklist.step: Review the completed schedule set against the inventory
actions: Walk the inventory row by row and confirm each schedule is present, complete, reconciled and signed off by its preparer and reviewer.
Read the interlock log and the reconciliation summaries and challenge any explanation that restates the difference instead of explaining it.
Compare each major schedule total to prior year and require a written cause for any movement above the review threshold.
Approve the set for filing and record the approval date on the inventory.
checklist.done: the Controller has approved a complete inventory with every schedule reconciled, interlocked and movement-explained.

checklist.step: Release the schedules with the annual statement and the 1 April supplements
actions: Include the annual schedules in the frozen statement version filed on 1 March and confirm the electronic file contains every schedule marked applicable.
Generate the 1 April supplemental filings from the same frozen version and confirm each supplement reconciles to the annual pages it derives from.
Upload each and capture the acceptance confirmation on its own inventory row.
Release the Japan annex forms with the Art. 110 report submission and capture the FSA receipt on the annex rows.
checklist.done: annual schedules, 1 April supplements and the Japan annex forms are all filed from the frozen version with per-row acceptance evidence.

checklist.step: Correct and refile any schedule error found after filing
actions: Log every post-filing schedule error with the schedule, the line, the amount and whether surplus or a filed total is affected.
Decide with the Controller and General Counsel whether an amended filing is required or whether the correction rolls into the next statement.
Where amended, refile the corrected schedule with the regulator and capture a new acceptance confirmation.
Record the root cause so the source extract or the mapping is fixed before the next annual cycle.
checklist.done: every post-filing schedule error has a logged amount, an amend-or-roll decision and, where amended, a new acceptance confirmation.

checklist.step: Archive the schedule evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the schedule file into the evidence repository under entity and business year: inventory, frozen extracts, reconciliations, interlock log, custodian and reinsurer confirmations and the filed schedules.
Apply the 10-year-from-business-year-end retention label to the whole file.
Confirm the record is searchable by schedule name, entity and business year so an examiner request can be answered from the index.
Close the schedule tasks in the close calendar only after the archive is confirmed.
checklist.done: the schedule evidence is archived under entity and business year, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by schedule name.

testing.step: Build the population of schedules owed and schedules filed
actions: Derive the schedules owed independently from the Annual Statement Instructions for the entity blank type and the ordinance annex form set.
Extract the schedules actually present in the filed statement version from the blanks software table of contents.
Compare the two lists and log every schedule owed but absent, and every schedule present without an inventory row.
Sign the population as complete with the instruction edition and the filed version identifier recorded.
testing.done: an independently derived schedules-owed list is compared to the filed set with every gap logged and the instruction edition recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile each sampled schedule to its frozen source extract
actions: Obtain the stamped source extract for each sampled schedule and independently total it on the fields the schedule reports.
Compare the independent total to the filed schedule total and to the ledger account balance behind it.
Investigate every difference and require a referenced explanation from the schedule owner rather than accepting a rounding claim.
Confirm the extract as-of date matches the statement period end and that the extract was taken after the ledger freeze.
testing.done: each sampled schedule total reconciles to an independently footed frozen extract and to the ledger, with differences referenced.

testing.step: Draw and document the schedule and security sample
actions: Take 100 percent of the asset schedules, the reinsurance schedules and the Japan Art. 115 annex.
Take 40 securities at random with a recorded seed across the bond, stock, acquisition and disposal schedules, weighted to the largest carrying values.
Take 15 reinsurer rows and 10 premiums-by-state rows at random with the same seed discipline.
Record the population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all asset and reinsurance schedules plus 40 securities, 15 reinsurers and 10 state rows is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the security-level detail against the custodian
actions: For each sampled security agree identifier, par or units, acquisition date, book or adjusted carrying value and fair value to the custodian statement at period end.
Re-derive the NAIC designation from the SVO listing or the filing-exempt rating in force at period end and compare it to the filed designation.
For sampled disposals, recompute the realized gain or loss as consideration less book value at disposal and compare to the filed amount.
Log any designation or valuation difference with the security identifier and the carrying amount affected.
testing.done: every sampled security agrees to the custodian on identifier, valuation and designation, with any realized-gain difference recomputed and logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the Art. 115 asset class split and rate application
actions: Independently classify the period-end asset base into the ordinance classes from the security master rather than from the annex sheet.
Apply the ordinance accumulation rate per class and recompute the required accrual and the ceiling.
Compare the recomputed class book values to the corresponding US schedule totals and confirm the annex cross-check explains any difference.
Log any misclassified asset with the amount and the effect on the required accrual.
testing.done: the ordinance class split, rate application and ceiling are independently recomputed and every misclassification is quantified.

testing.step: Test reinsurance recoverables against confirmations and status
actions: For each sampled reinsurer, agree the recoverable balance to the returned confirmation and to the ceded accounting subledger.
Independently verify the authorised or unauthorised status against the domiciliary state listing rather than the internal flag.
Recompute the provision for reinsurance on unauthorised and aged balances and compare to the posted provision.
Log any reinsurer with no confirmation, a stale status flag, or an understated provision.
testing.done: sampled recoverables agree to confirmations, statuses are independently verified, and the provision is recomputed with differences logged.

testing.step: Recompute the interlocks between schedules and the financial pages
actions: Open the filed statement version and independently total each sampled schedule, then compare it to the page line it is required to support.
Compare your results to the interlock log kept in the close file and investigate any interlock that appears clean in the log but fails on recomputation.
Read each permitted-difference explanation and judge whether it identifies the cause and the amount.
Log any broken interlock left open at filing with the schedule, page, line and amount.
testing.done: each sampled interlock is independently recomputed, log entries are corroborated, and open breaks are logged with amounts.

testing.step: Verify the premiums-by-state allocation and the licence coverage
actions: For each sampled state row, re-extract direct written premium from policy administration using the situs rule the instructions prescribe.
Compare the re-extracted amount to the filed schedule row and quantify any difference.
Cross-check every state showing premium against the certificate of authority register and flag any state with premium but no active licence for that line.
Escalate any unlicensed-writing indication to Regulatory Counsel the same day.
testing.done: sampled state premium is re-extracted and compared, and any premium written in a state without an active licence is escalated same day.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the schedule, the line, the amount, the entity and the effect on a filed total or on surplus.
Assign a root cause from the standard set: stale extract, custodian break, designation error, misclassification, allocation rule error, or missing schedule.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and record whether an amended schedule filing is required.
Carry every open exception into next year's schedule test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception carries a tracked issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and an amended-filing decision.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the schedule verification
actions: Compute the exception rate by schedule and by sampled security and compare it to the zero-unexplained-difference threshold.
Write the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper reference behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and reviewed no sampled schedule, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any unlicensed-writing indication and any amended filings to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the exception rate, a stated conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.
