checklist.step: Confirm auditor appointment and test independence before fieldwork
actions: Confirm the Audit Committee resolution appointing the audit firm for the year is minuted, with the lead engagement partner named and the partner rotation period tracked.
Obtain the firm's written independence confirmation covering the firm, the engagement team and any affiliate, referencing the applicable independence rules.
Collect the schedule of non-audit services provided or proposed, with fees, and confirm each was pre-approved by the Audit Committee before it started.
File the resolution, the confirmation and the pre-approval schedule to the board portal record for the audit year.
checklist.done: a minuted appointment, a written independence confirmation and a pre-approved non-audit service schedule exist before fieldwork opens.

checklist.step: Agree the audit timetable against the statutory filing dates
actions: Work backwards from the 1 June audited financial report date and the Japan accounting auditor report date to set fieldwork, clearance and opinion dates.
Agree the interim fieldwork window, the hard-close date, the PBC delivery dates and the audit committee clearance meeting date with the engagement partner in writing.
Load every milestone into the audit tool with an owner and confirm the dates leave at least 10 business days between opinion and filing.
Circulate the timetable to Financial Reporting, Actuarial, Investment Accounting and Reinsurance Accounting.
checklist.done: a written timetable exists with milestone owners and at least 10 business days between the opinion date and each statutory filing date.

checklist.step: Own the PBC list line by line
actions: Load the auditor PBC request list into the audit tool and assign every line to a named preparer with a due date ahead of the auditor need-by date.
Reject vague requests back to the auditor for specification rather than guessing what evidence satisfies them.
Set the evidence standard on each line: source system, extract parameters, as-of date and the reconciliation it must carry.
Run a weekly PBC status call and escalate any line more than 2 business days late to the Controller.
checklist.done: every PBC line has a named preparer, a due date, a defined evidence standard and a weekly-tracked status.

checklist.step: Deliver the reserve and price fluctuation reserve substantiation
actions: Provide the auditor with the valuation basis documentation, the in-force reconciliation, the reserve roll-forward and the asset adequacy analysis for the year.
Provide the Art. 116 policy reserve and Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve derivations tied to the filed tables.
Provide the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve calculation with the asset class split, the ordinance rates applied, the ceiling test and any drawdown support.
Answer auditor and reviewing actuary queries in writing and keep the query log in the audit tool rather than in mailboxes.
checklist.done: reserve and Art. 115 substantiation is delivered with a written query log and every derivation tied to a filed table.

checklist.step: Support the auditor walkthroughs and control testing
actions: Schedule walkthroughs for the significant processes: statutory close, reserving, investment valuation, reinsurance ceding, and premium recognition.
Provide the current process narratives, control matrices and the population and sample evidence for each key control tested internally.
Where the auditor plans to rely on internal work, provide the internal testing workpapers and the tester independence evidence.
Log each control exception the auditor raises with the control identifier, the deficiency severity and the process owner the same week.
checklist.done: walkthroughs are completed for every significant process and each auditor-raised control exception is logged with severity and owner.

checklist.step: Run the audit adjustment protocol
actions: Maintain a single schedule of audit differences with the amount, the account, whether it is a factual, judgemental or projected difference, and the surplus effect.
Decide record or pass on each difference with the Chief Financial Officer, and record the rationale, never leaving a difference undecided.
Recompute the aggregate effect of passed differences on surplus and on the risk-based capital ratio before agreeing to pass them.
Post recorded adjustments as numbered journals in the ledger and reissue the affected statement pages from the revised trial balance.
checklist.done: every audit difference is recorded or passed with a written rationale, and the aggregate passed effect on surplus and RBC is quantified.

checklist.step: Assemble and sign the management representation letter
actions: Work each representation against evidence: completeness of records, related party transactions, litigation and claims from Legal Counsel, subsequent events, and the reserve basis from the Appointed Actuary.
Obtain the written support for the litigation and claims representation directly from General Counsel before signing.
Confirm the representation letter is dated the same date as the audit opinion and references the exact financial statements being opined on.
Have the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer sign and file the executed letter with the audit file.
checklist.done: a signed representation letter dated with the opinion exists, with written Legal and Actuarial support behind the litigation and reserve representations.

checklist.step: Clear the audit at the Audit Committee
actions: Circulate the draft audited statements, the auditor report to the committee, the schedule of passed differences and the control deficiency list ahead of the meeting.
Minute the auditor private session with the committee, held without management present.
Minute the committee resolution approving the audited financial statements and authorising their filing.
File the pack and the minutes in the board portal under the audit year.
checklist.done: the committee has resolved to approve and authorise filing, with the private session and the passed-difference discussion minuted.

checklist.step: Obtain the signed opinion and the audited financial statements
actions: Receive the signed audit opinion and check the opinion type, the entity name, the period covered and the basis of accounting stated in it.
Confirm the audited statements attached to the opinion are the version the Audit Committee approved, page for page.
Reconcile the audited statutory figures to the filed annual statement and document any difference and its treatment.
Store the signed opinion and statements in the financial reporting repository under the entity and audit year.
checklist.done: a signed opinion of the expected type is held with statements matching the committee-approved version and reconciled to the filed statement.

checklist.step: File the audited financial report with each regulator
actions: File the audited financial report with the domiciliary regulator by 1 June and with every other state that requires a copy, using the channel that state accepts.
Submit the Japan accounting auditor report with the Art. 110 business report package through the FSA electronic notification channel.
Capture the regulator-side receipt for each filing and record it on the filing matrix row.
Where an extension is needed, request it in writing before the due date and file the granted extension with the receipt evidence.
checklist.done: the audited report is receipted by every required regulator by its due date, or a written extension granted before the due date is on file.

checklist.step: File the internal control communications on time
actions: Collect the auditor communication of internal control related matters and file it with the domiciliary regulator by 1 August.
Where the entity meets the premium threshold, assemble and file management's report on internal control over financial reporting by the same date.
Confirm the report covers the controls over statutory financial reporting and names the framework used to evaluate them.
Capture the receipt for each communication on the filing matrix row.
checklist.done: the auditor internal control communication and, where required, management's report are receipted by the regulator by 1 August.

checklist.step: Remediate the deficiencies the auditor raised
actions: Log every deficiency with its severity as assessed by the auditor: control deficiency, significant deficiency or material weakness.
Assign a process owner and a remediation date proportionate to severity, with material weaknesses due before the next hard close.
Require the owner to evidence the remediated control operating at least twice before the deficiency is closed.
Report open significant deficiencies and material weaknesses to the Audit Committee at every meeting until closed.
checklist.done: every deficiency has a severity, an owner, a remediation date and evidence of the remediated control operating before closure.

checklist.step: Assess the audit firm and plan the next cycle
actions: Score the engagement on timetable adherence, quality of findings, industry expertise and fee against scope, using input from the Controller and the Appointed Actuary.
Check the lead partner rotation clock and flag the year in which rotation becomes mandatory.
Present the assessment and the reappointment recommendation to the Audit Committee with the proposed fee.
Record the committee decision and open the next cycle's engagement letter and independence process.
checklist.done: a documented firm assessment, rotation clock position and a committee reappointment decision exist before the next cycle opens.

checklist.step: Publish the audited results into the disclosure and governance pack
actions: Provide the audited statements and the opinion to the team preparing the public explanatory disclosure documents that accompany the Art. 110 reporting cycle.
Confirm the figures quoted in the disclosure documents match the audited statements line for line.
Record the board approval of the disclosure documents in the minutes with the approval date.
File the approved disclosure documents with the audit year record.
checklist.done: the disclosure documents quote audited figures line for line and their board approval is minuted and filed.

checklist.step: Archive the audit evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the audit file into the evidence repository under entity and audit year: engagement letter, independence confirmation, PBC log, adjustment schedule, representation letter, opinion, statements and filing receipts.
Apply the 10-year-from-audit-year-end retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by entity, audit year and audit firm.
Close the audit cycle tasks in the audit tool only after the archive is confirmed.
checklist.done: the full audit file is archived under entity and audit year, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by entity and firm.

testing.step: Build the population of audit engagements and required audit filings
actions: List every entity required to file an audited financial report, derived from the licence register rather than from last year's filing list.

For each, list the audit deliverables owed: audited report by 1 June, internal control communication by 1 August, management's report where the premium threshold is met, and the Japan accounting auditor report.
Determine the premium threshold test for each entity from the filed annual statement premium line to establish whether management's report is owed.
Sign the population as complete with the source registers and the threshold calculation recorded.
testing.done: the population lists every entity, every owed audit deliverable and a recomputed premium-threshold determination.

testing.step: Verify auditor independence evidence for the cycle
actions: Obtain the firm independence confirmation and check it is dated in the audit year and names the engagement team scope.
Extract every payment to the audit firm and its affiliates from accounts payable for the year and reconcile it to the non-audit services schedule.
For each non-audit service, confirm a dated Audit Committee pre-approval that pre-dates the service start, not a retrospective ratification.
Check the lead partner rotation record against the mandatory rotation period and log any breach.
testing.done: every payment to the firm reconciles to a pre-approved service and the partner rotation clock is verified against the mandatory period.

testing.step: Draw and document the PBC and adjustment sample
actions: Take 100 percent of audit adjustments, both recorded and passed, and 100 percent of raised control deficiencies.
Take 30 PBC lines at random with a recorded seed, stratified across Financial Reporting, Actuarial, Investment Accounting and Reinsurance Accounting.
Record the population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every PBC line delivered more than 5 business days late as a mandatory sample item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all adjustments and deficiencies plus 30 stratified PBC lines and every very late line is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the audit adjustment surplus and RBC effect
actions: Recompute the aggregate effect of all passed differences on statutory surplus, treating each difference in the direction the auditor identified.
Recompute the risk-based capital ratio with the passed differences recorded and compare it to the filed ratio and to the regulator action levels.
Confirm every recorded adjustment traces to a numbered ledger journal and that the reissued statement pages reflect it.
Log any passed difference that would move the entity into or nearer an action level as a reportable exception.
testing.done: the aggregate passed-difference effect on surplus and RBC is independently recomputed and any action-level impact is reported.

testing.step: Test the reserve and Art. 115 substantiation the auditor relied on
actions: Obtain the reserve roll-forward and the Art. 115 calculation supplied to the auditor and agree them to the valuation output and the investment accounting balances.
Confirm the in-force reconciliation supplied to the auditor uses the same extract as the filed statement, with no later refresh.
Re-apply the ordinance rate per asset class to the Art. 115 base and confirm the number the auditor tested is the number that was filed.
Log any difference between the substantiation pack and the filed tables with the amount.
testing.done: the substantiation given to the auditor is agreed to the valuation and investment records and to the filed tables, with differences logged.

testing.step: Recompute the audit filing deadlines and test timeliness
actions: Recompute each due date from the statute: 1 June for the audited report, 1 August for the internal control communication and management's report, and the Art. 110 date for the Japan accounting auditor report.
Compare each recomputed date to the regulator-side receipt timestamp and compute days early or late.
Where an extension was used, confirm the written request pre-dates the due date and the grant is in the file.
List every late filing with the entity, the deliverable and the days late.
testing.done: days early or late is computed for every audit deliverable against a recomputed due date, with extensions verified as pre-dated and granted.

testing.step: Trace the opinion to the approved and filed statements
actions: Compare the statements attached to the signed opinion against the version minuted as approved by the Audit Committee, page by page on the primary statements.
Compare the audited statutory figures to the annual statement as filed and confirm every difference is documented and explained.
Confirm the opinion date, the representation letter date and the committee approval date are consistent and none post-dates the filing.
Log any version mismatch as an exception regardless of whether the amounts differ.
testing.done: the opinion, the approved statements and the filed statement are proven to be the same version with dates in a defensible order.

testing.step: Test deficiency remediation for evidence of operation
actions: For each significant deficiency and material weakness, obtain the remediation evidence and confirm the redesigned control has operated at least twice.
Re-perform the control on one instance yourself rather than reading the owner's assertion.
Confirm the closure date and the Chief Audit Executive sign-off exist and pre-date the closure in the tool.
Log any deficiency closed without operating evidence as an exception and reopen it.
testing.done: every closed significant deficiency has re-performed operating evidence and a pre-dated sign-off, or is reopened.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the entity, the deliverable or adjustment, the amount and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the standard set: independence lapse, late PBC, unsupported passed difference, version mismatch, late filing, or premature deficiency closure.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and escalate any independence or material weakness exception to the Audit Committee chair immediately.
Carry every open exception into the next audit cycle test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has a tracked issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, with independence and material weakness items escalated immediately.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the audit cycle test
actions: Compute the on-time rate for audit deliverables and the count of unresolved independence and passed-difference exceptions against the thresholds.
Write the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper reference behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no PBC item and negotiated no adjustment, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next meeting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the on-time rate, exception counts, a stated conclusion and the committee reporting date is in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager owns the multi-jurisdiction filing calendar and the timeliness evidence; Corporate Secretary owns the shareholder and control-event entries that sit on it

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Insurance Business Act Art. 271-10 (major shareholder approval at the 20 percent voting-rights threshold, 15 percent under the influence test) verified against the current FSA text, together with each jurisdiction's own filing calendar source: NAIC Annual Statement Instructions filing checklist and state bulletins

In-scope processes.value: Maintenance of the enterprise regulatory filing calendar across every licensed jurisdiction: recurring statutory, actuarial, market conduct and holding company filings, plus event-driven entries such as an Art. 271-10 major shareholder approval and any change of control

In-scope systems.value: Calendar entries, owners, due dates, submission receipts and the timeliness dashboard held in the regulatory obligations register, with source authority documents attached per entry

Compliance procedure documented.value: Regulatory Filing Calendar Procedure - entry creation from a cited source, owner assignment, reminder cadence, receipt capture, event-driven entry triggers, and quarterly recertification of the whole calendar

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; reviewed quarterly at recertification and immediately on a new licence, a surrendered licence, or a control event under Art. 271-10

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Every recurring due date in the register, refreshed each January from the reissued instructions; event-driven entries dated from the trigger event, including the Art. 271-10 approval which must be obtained before the shareholder crosses the threshold

Deadline reminders configured.value: Standing reminders at 30, 14, 5 and 1 days before each due date to the entry owner and the Regulatory Reporting Manager; event-driven entries alert daily from creation until receipted

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Calendar snapshots at each quarter end, the source authority attached to each entry, submission receipts and the recertification sign-offs, retained 10 years from the filing year

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missing calendar entries found after the fact, entries with no cited source, filings receipted after the due date and any threshold crossing that occurred before approval are logged with the jurisdiction and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every missed filing remediation and every calendar entry added retrospectively

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every calendar entry with a due date in the period across all licensed jurisdictions, plus every event-driven entry raised in the period including Art. 271-10 shareholder approvals and control filings

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100 percent of calendar entries carry a cited source and a named owner, zero entries pass their due date without a receipt, zero recurring obligations discovered outside the calendar, zero threshold crossings without a prior approval

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; completeness and timeliness testing runs quarterly against that quarter's due dates, with the full calendar recertified annually against reissued instructions

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not own any calendar entry in the sample nor have performed any of the sampled submissions

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly filing calendar test workpaper (calendar extract, independent obligation derivation, receipt tracing, deadline recomputation) in the compliance evidence repository under the quarter

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Calendar extract by jurisdiction with due dates, submission dates and receipts, plus the Art. 271-10 approval file, producible to an FSA inspection or a state market conduct or financial examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager answers examiner questions on filing history and timeliness; Corporate Secretary and General Counsel handle FSA correspondence on major shareholder approval and control events

checklist.step: Rebuild the jurisdiction inventory from the licence register
actions: Extract every live licence from the corporate licence register: entity, jurisdiction, licence or certificate of authority number, lines of authority and issue date.
Add the Japan FSA licence with its business category and the entities registered under it.
Remove jurisdictions where the licence was surrendered or lapsed, recording the surrender date so the calendar stops generating entries after it.
Publish the inventory to the Regulatory Reporting Manager as the authoritative jurisdiction list for calendar building.
checklist.done: a dated jurisdiction inventory lists every live licence with entity, number, lines and issue date, and every surrender with its date.

checklist.step: Derive the recurring obligations for each jurisdiction from a cited source
actions: For each jurisdiction on the inventory, read the current filing checklist, statute or bulletin that sets the recurring obligations and list each one.
For Japan, list the Art. 110 business report, the reserve annexes under Art. 115 to Art. 117, the solvency margin submission and the explanatory disclosure documents.
Record on every derived obligation the citation, the source document title and the date it was read.
Reject any obligation entered without a citation - the source is the entry, not a memory of past practice.
checklist.done: every recurring obligation carries a citation, a source document title and a read date for its jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Create calendar entries with owners and computed due dates
actions: Create one register entry per obligation per entity per jurisdiction with the frequency, the due-date rule and the computed next due date.
Encode the rule rather than the date, so the calendar recomputes each cycle: fixed calendar date, days after period end, or days after a trigger event.
Assign a named owner and a named backup from the responsible team and require both to accept the entry in the register.
Set the internal target date ahead of the statutory date by the preparation lead time agreed with the owner.
checklist.done: every obligation is a register entry with an encoded due-date rule, a computed due date, an accepted owner and an internal target date.

checklist.step: Configure the reminder and escalation cadence
actions: Set reminders on each entry at 30, 14, 5 and 1 days before the statutory due date, addressed to the owner and copied to the backup.
Set the escalation rule so an entry still open at due date minus 1 day notifies the Regulatory Reporting Manager, and at due date the Head of Compliance.
Test the reminder configuration by forcing a test entry through the cadence and confirming each notification lands.
Record the reminder configuration on the entry so an examiner can see the control, not just the outcome.
checklist.done: each entry shows a tested reminder cadence and an escalation rule that reaches the Head of Compliance on the due date.

checklist.step: Trigger event-driven entries for shareholder and control events
actions: Monitor the shareholder register and any share transfer, subscription or option exercise that moves a holder's voting rights toward the Art. 271-10 thresholds.
Where a holder will reach 20 percent, or 15 percent with an influence factor, raise a calendar entry for the FSA major shareholder approval that must be obtained before the crossing occurs.
Raise the parallel entries the same event triggers in other jurisdictions, such as a change of control approval filing with the domiciliary regulator.
Notify General Counsel and the Head of Compliance the day the trigger is identified and record the notification on the entry.
checklist.done: every approaching threshold crossing has a dated entry for the prior FSA approval and the parallel jurisdiction filings, with Legal notified the same day.

checklist.step: Support the major shareholder approval filing
actions: Assemble the information the FSA requires from the prospective major shareholder: identity, shareholding structure, funding source, financial statements and the purpose of the holding.
Prepare the insurer-side supporting statement covering the group structure, governance arrangements and the effect of the holding on the insurer.
Track the FSA review through to the approval decision and record the decision date on the calendar entry.
Confirm with the Corporate Secretary that no share transfer is registered that would cross the threshold before the approval date.
checklist.done: the approval application is filed with full shareholder and insurer-side support and no threshold-crossing transfer is registered before the approval date.

checklist.step: Run the weekly calendar review with the owners
actions: Produce the 60-day forward view from the register showing entries due, owner, status and internal target date.
Walk each amber and red entry with its owner and record the blocker, the recovery action and the recovery date on the entry.
Escalate any entry that cannot meet its statutory date to the Head of Compliance the same day, with the options written out.
Circulate the reviewed forward view to the Controller, the Head of Compliance and the affected owners.
checklist.done: a weekly reviewed 60-day forward view exists with a recorded blocker and recovery action against every amber and red entry.

checklist.step: Capture the submission receipt against every closed entry
actions: Require the owner to attach the regulator-side receipt to the entry before its status can move to complete.
Record the regulator receipt timestamp, not the internal send time, and compare it to the statutory due date on the entry.
Reject completion where the only evidence is an internal email or a preparer assertion, and return the entry to open.
Run a daily report of entries marked complete without an attached receipt and clear it to zero.
checklist.done: no entry reaches complete status without an attached regulator receipt and a recorded regulator-side timestamp.

checklist.step: Recertify the whole calendar every quarter
actions: Send every owner their entries and require a written confirmation that the obligation, frequency, due-date rule and owner are still correct.
Compare the entry count to the jurisdiction inventory and investigate any jurisdiction with no entries or an implausibly small set.
Snapshot the calendar at quarter end and store the snapshot as evidence of the register's state at that date.
Record non-responding owners as an exception and escalate to their department head.
checklist.done: every entry carries a quarterly owner recertification and a quarter-end calendar snapshot is stored as evidence.

checklist.step: Refresh the calendar from reissued regulatory sources
actions: Each January read the reissued NAIC filing checklist and each state's bulletin list, and each FSA ordinance amendment cycle, and mark every changed requirement.
Update the affected entries' due-date rules, forms and channels, and update the citation and read date on each changed entry.
Create entries for new obligations and retire entries for obligations withdrawn, recording the authority for the retirement.
Brief the owners on the changes affecting their entries before the first affected due date.
checklist.done: the calendar is refreshed annually with an updated citation and read date on every changed entry and retirements authority-backed.

checklist.step: Add and retire entries when licences change
actions: On a new licence, derive the jurisdiction's recurring obligations from its filing checklist and create the entries before the first business is written there.
On a surrendered licence, confirm the final filings due after surrender are still on the calendar before retiring the recurring entries.
On a change of lines of authority, review which obligations attach only to specific lines and adjust the entries.
Record the licence event, its date and the entries created or retired on the change log.
checklist.done: every licence change has a dated change-log record showing the entries created or retired and the final filings preserved.

checklist.step: Publish the timeliness dashboard to leadership
actions: Build the dashboard from the register showing on-time rate by jurisdiction and by owner, open entries past due, and entries missing a receipt.
Show the trailing four quarters so a deteriorating jurisdiction or owner is visible rather than averaged away.
Circulate the dashboard monthly to the Head of Compliance, the Chief Financial Officer and the General Counsel.
Present any past-due entry with its jurisdiction, days overdue, cause and the named recovery owner.
checklist.done: a monthly dashboard shows on-time rate by jurisdiction and owner over four quarters with every past-due entry named and owned.

checklist.step: Work missed filings to a self-report decision
actions: On any filing receipted after its statutory due date, open an issue capturing the jurisdiction, entity, filing, due date, actual date and days late.
Assess with General Counsel whether the jurisdiction requires notification of the late filing or imposes a penalty, and record the assessment.
File the late submission immediately and, where required, the accompanying explanation to the regulator.
Fix the calendar cause - wrong rule, no owner, missing entry - before the issue is closed.
checklist.done: every late filing has a days-late measure, a self-report assessment with Legal, a completed submission and a fixed calendar cause.

checklist.step: Prepare the examination-ready calendar extract
actions: Build a standing extract per jurisdiction showing each obligation, its citation, due dates for the examination period, submission dates and receipt references.
Attach the receipts as an indexed appendix so a single filing can be produced without a search.
Refresh the extract quarterly so the pack is never more than one quarter stale when an examination is announced.
Confirm the extract can be produced for any single jurisdiction within 5 business days of a request.
checklist.done: a per-jurisdiction extract with citations, dates and indexed receipts is refreshed quarterly and producible within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Archive the calendar evidence for the retention period
actions: Move each quarter-end calendar snapshot, the recertification responses, the change log and the receipt index into the evidence repository under the year and quarter.
Apply the 10-year-from-filing-year retention label so the record survives an examination lookback.
Confirm the record is searchable by jurisdiction, entity, obligation and due date.
Record the archive date on the quarterly recertification record.
checklist.done: quarterly snapshots, recertifications, change log and receipt index are archived, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by jurisdiction.

testing.step: Derive the expected obligation population independently of the register
actions: Take the licence register from the Corporate Secretary and, for a selected set of jurisdictions, read the current filing checklist or statute directly.
List the obligations each jurisdiction imposes on the entity for the period without looking at the regulatory register first.
Add the Japan obligations derived from the Insurance Business Act and its ordinance, including the Art. 271-10 approval where a threshold event occurred.
Sign the derived list with the sources and read dates recorded.
testing.done: an independently derived obligation list exists for the selected jurisdictions with sources and read dates recorded.

testing.step: Test the calendar for completeness against the derived list
actions: Match each derived obligation to a register entry on entity, jurisdiction, obligation and frequency.
List every derived obligation with no register entry as a completeness failure, and quantify how many due dates it would have missed in the period.
List every register entry not on the derived list and confirm it is a genuine obligation rather than a duplicate.
Check that every entry carries a citation and a read date, and log entries citing nothing.
testing.done: every derived obligation is matched to an entry or logged as a completeness failure with its missed due-date count.

testing.step: Draw and document the timeliness sample
actions: Take 100 percent of entries due in the quarter for the domiciliary jurisdictions and 100 percent of event-driven entries including Art. 271-10 approvals.
Take 40 entries at random with a recorded seed from the remaining due-in-quarter population, spread across owners.
Record the population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample is reproducible.
Add every entry that was reopened or had its due date changed during the quarter as a mandatory sample item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all domiciliary and event-driven entries plus 40 random entries and every date-changed entry is documented.

testing.step: Recompute the due date on each sampled entry
actions: Read the cited source on each sampled entry and independently apply its due-date rule to the period to derive the date.
Compare your derived date to the register due date and log any entry where the encoded rule produces a later date than the statute allows.
Check weekend and public holiday rolling was applied the way the source prescribes, including the Japan holiday calendar for FSA submissions.
Treat a permissive rule error as an exception even where the filing happened to be on time.
testing.done: each sampled due date is independently recomputed from the cited source and every permissive rule error is logged.

testing.step: Trace each sampled entry to a regulator-side receipt
actions: Open the receipt attached to each sampled completed entry and read the regulator-side timestamp, the entity and the filing named on it.
Confirm the receipt belongs to the obligation on the entry and not to a different filing in the same jurisdiction.
Compare the receipt timestamp to the recomputed due date and compute days early or late.
Log any entry marked complete whose evidence is an internal email, a screenshot without a timestamp, or a preparer assertion.
testing.done: every sampled entry traces to a matching regulator receipt with a timestamp compared to the recomputed due date.

testing.step: Re-perform the Art. 271-10 threshold test on the shareholder register
actions: Obtain the shareholder register movements for the period and independently compute each holder's voting-rights percentage after each movement.
Identify every holder that reached or exceeded 20 percent, and every holder at or above 15 percent where an influence factor such as board representation or a funding relationship exists.
For each identified holder, confirm an FSA approval decision dated before the transfer was registered.
Treat any crossing registered before approval as a reportable statutory breach, not a calendar exception.
testing.done: voting-rights percentages are independently recomputed after each movement and every crossing is proven to post-date its FSA approval.

testing.step: Test the reminder and escalation control end to end
actions: Select 10 sampled entries and pull the notification history from the register for each.
Confirm the 30, 14, 5 and 1 day reminders fired to the named owner and backup and that the due-date escalation reached the Head of Compliance where the entry stayed open.
For entries where reminders did not fire, determine whether the configuration was missing or the notification failed, and log which.
Confirm that owner changes during the period carried the reminders to the new owner.
testing.done: notification histories prove the reminder cadence and escalation operated on each tested entry, with failures classified as configuration or delivery.

testing.step: Test recertification and refresh evidence
actions: Obtain the quarter-end calendar snapshot and confirm it was taken at quarter end rather than reconstructed later.
Check each sampled entry carries an owner recertification for the quarter with a name and a date.
Compare the January refresh evidence to at least three reissued source documents and confirm the affected entries were actually updated.
Log entries whose citation read date is more than 12 months old as stale.
testing.done: quarter-end snapshots, dated owner recertifications and the annual refresh are evidenced, with stale citations logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the jurisdiction, entity, obligation, due date, receipt date and the days late or the completeness gap.
Assign a root cause from the standard set: missing entry, wrong due-date rule, no owner, reminder not configured, receipt not captured, or unapproved threshold crossing.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and open a self-report assessment with General Counsel for any missed statutory filing or unapproved crossing.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's calendar test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has a tracked issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a self-report assessment where statutory.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the calendar test
actions: Compute the calendar completeness rate and the on-time filing rate for the quarter and compare both to the 100 percent thresholds.
Write the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper reference behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no sampled entry and performed no sampled submission, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, missed filings and any Art. 271-10 breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with completeness and on-time rates, a stated conclusion and the committee reporting date is in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager owns the authority-to-write gate; Corporate Secretary holds the certificates and Regulatory Counsel clears every close call before business is bound

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Insurance Business Act Art. 3(1) (licence required before carrying on insurance business) and Art. 315 (penalty for unlicensed business), with Art. 123 and Art. 125 (prior approval or notification before changing the statement of business procedures, policy conditions or premium and reserve calculation methods) re-read at each market or product entry; US authority verified against the state certificate of authority and the statutory line classification

In-scope processes.value: Pre-market-entry authority gate: verifying the certificate of authority or FSA licence covers the entity, the jurisdiction and the exact line of business, and confirming the Art. 123 approval or notification for the business procedures and calculation-method documents before any policy is bound

In-scope systems.value: Authority matrix enforced as a bind-time control in the underwriting platform, sourced from the licence register and the certificate images

Compliance procedure documented.value: Authority to Write Verification Procedure - certificate lookup by entity, jurisdiction and line, Art. 123 change-category determination, expansion application route where authority is missing, and the bind-time block until authority is proven

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel; reviewed on every new market entry, licence amendment and any FSA ordinance change to the Art. 123 change categories

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per market entry - the authority check must close before the first bind date; where an Art. 123 prior approval is required the FSA review period drives the earliest launch date, and a notification-category change must be filed before use

Deadline reminders configured.value: Launch-plan milestones at 120, 90 and 30 days before the target first-bind date on every pending authority or Art. 123 item, with an automatic hold on the launch gate until each closes

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Certificate of authority images with line schedules, FSA licence and approval or notification receipts, the change-category determination memo and counsel clearance, retained 10 years from the date the entity stops writing the line

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any policy bound in a jurisdiction or line the certificate does not cover, and any product change used before its Art. 123 approval or notification, is logged as a breach with the premium and policy count affected

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Regulatory Counsel signs off every authority determination that permits a launch and every unlicensed-writing remediation

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every market entry approved in the period plus every policy bound in the period grouped by entity, jurisdiction and statutory line, and every Art. 123 change put into use

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero policies bound in an entity, jurisdiction or line combination not covered by a live certificate, zero Art. 123 changes used before their approval or notification date; any single breach escalates to the Head of Compliance and General Counsel

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is a per-market-entry gate; the gate is tested on every entry and the bound-policy population is tested quarterly against the certificate register

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have made or approved any sampled authority determination

Evidence location for test results.value: Authority verification workpaper (bound-policy population, certificate register extract, coverage matching results, Art. 123 date tracing) in the compliance evidence repository under the quarter

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Certificate images with line schedules, the FSA licence and Art. 123 approval and notification receipts, and the bound-policy to authority reconciliation, producible to a market conduct examination or an FSA inspection within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager answers licensing questions from state departments; General Counsel handles any FSA correspondence touching Art. 3 or Art. 315 exposure and clears any admission of unlicensed writing

checklist.step: Take in the market entry request and define the exact scope
actions: Record the proposed writing entity, the target jurisdictions, the statutory lines and sub-lines, the product and the target first-bind date.
State whether the business will be written on an admitted basis, through a branch, or via a fronting or reinsurance arrangement, since each changes the authority needed.
Name the distribution channel and confirm whether producers will solicit in that jurisdiction, which triggers the separate producer licensing path.
Submit the request to the Regulatory Affairs Manager and hold the launch plan until the authority gate closes.
checklist.done: the request names entity, jurisdictions, statutory lines, basis of writing, channel and target first-bind date, and the launch plan is held.

checklist.step: Pull the current certificate of authority for each entity and jurisdiction
actions: Retrieve the certificate of authority image for each target jurisdiction from the corporate record, including any amendment or endorsement pages.
Read the effective date, the expiry or continuous-renewal status and the exact lines of authority listed, and note the statutory line names the state uses.
Where the certificate on file is more than 12 months old or its status is unclear, request a certificate of compliance or current status letter from the department.
Retrieve the FSA licence document and the registered business categories for the Japan entity.
checklist.done: a current certificate image with its line schedule and status is on file for every target jurisdiction and entity.

checklist.step: Map the product to the jurisdiction's statutory line names
actions: Translate the internal product classification into the statutory line name each jurisdiction uses, since a product may sit under a differently named line state by state.
For the Japan entity map the product to the licensed business category and confirm it falls inside the scope of the Art. 3 licence held.
Record on the mapping the source used - the state's line-of-authority list, the certificate schedule or the ordinance category list - with the date read.
Flag any product that maps to more than one line, since partial authority is the common failure mode.
checklist.done: each product is mapped to the named statutory line in every jurisdiction with a cited source, and multi-line products are flagged.

checklist.step: Test the certificate against the mapped line for every combination
actions: Build the matrix of entity by jurisdiction by mapped line and mark each cell covered, not covered, or unclear.
For covered cells attach the certificate page that names the line, not the certificate cover sheet.
For unclear cells write to the department's company licensing contact and record the question, the date and the answer received.
Escalate every not-covered cell to the launch decision as either an expansion application or a jurisdiction dropped from the launch.
checklist.done: every entity, jurisdiction and line cell is marked covered with an attached certificate page, or routed to expansion or exclusion.

checklist.step: Determine the Art. 123 change category for the product documents
actions: Identify which of the three Art. 5(1) documents the launch changes: the statement of business procedures, the general policy conditions, or the statement of calculation methods for premiums and policy reserves.
Determine the change category under Art. 123 and the implementing ordinance: prior approval, prior notification, or no filing, and write the reasoning with the ordinance reference.
Where a calculation-method change is involved, obtain the Appointed Actuary's written confirmation of the actuarial basis and the reserve effect.
Route the determination to Regulatory Counsel for clearance before any filing or launch date is fixed.
checklist.done: each changed Art. 5(1) document has a written change-category determination with an ordinance reference and counsel clearance pending.

checklist.step: File the Art. 123 approval application or notification
actions: Assemble the filing set: the marked-up statement of business procedures, policy conditions or calculation-method document, the rationale, and the actuarial support where reserves are affected.
Submit through the FSA electronic application and notification channel under the correct category, since a notification filed where approval is required does not cure the defect.
Track the FSA review, log every question received and the answer given with dates, and record the approval or acceptance date on the launch plan.
Do not release the launch gate until the approval date, or for notification categories the confirmed filing date, is recorded.
checklist.done: the Art. 123 filing is submitted in the correct category and the approval or notification date is recorded against the launch gate.

checklist.step: Run the expansion application where authority is missing
actions: For each not-covered jurisdiction, assemble the uniform expansion application set: the application form, the plan of operation, the certificate of compliance from the domiciliary state, audited financials and the biographical affidavits with third-party verification.
Check the state's own supplement requirements on the uniform chart of filing requirements, since state-specific items are the usual cause of rejection.
Submit with the correct fee and deposit requirement and track the department's review through to the certificate issue date.
Record the expected certificate date on the launch plan and treat it as a hard gate, not a target.
checklist.done: an expansion application is filed with the full uniform set and state supplements, and the expected certificate date is a hard gate on the launch plan.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Counsel clearance on the authority position
actions: Review every covered determination, reading the certificate line schedule and the mapping source rather than accepting the matrix cell.
Review the Art. 123 change-category determination against the current ordinance and confirm or overturn the category in writing.
State in writing that the entity may lawfully write the mapped lines in each jurisdiction from the stated date, or name the conditions still outstanding.
Record that unlicensed business exposes the entity to the Art. 315 penalty, so no conditional launch is permitted on an open cell.
checklist.done: counsel has cleared or overturned every authority and change-category determination in writing, with no launch on an open cell.

checklist.step: Load the authority matrix into the bind-time control
actions: Configure the entity, jurisdiction and line combinations cleared for writing, each with its earliest permitted bind date.
Set the rule to block quote issue and bind where the combination is absent, and to require an override with a named approver where it is present but dated in the future.
Test the block by attempting a bind in a jurisdiction and line not on the matrix and confirming the transaction is refused.
Record the configuration change with the effective date and the approver in the change log.
checklist.done: the platform refuses a test bind outside the cleared matrix and every cleared combination carries an earliest permitted bind date.

checklist.step: Align policy forms and rates to the cleared authority
actions: Confirm the forms and rates to be used in each jurisdiction have their own filing disposition recorded, since authority to write does not substitute for product approval.
Record the filing tracking number and approval or acceptance date for each jurisdiction on the launch plan.
Confirm the product coding used on the filing matches the statutory line the certificate covers.
Report any jurisdiction where authority is cleared but the product filing is not, so the launch gate stays closed for that jurisdiction.
checklist.done: each jurisdiction shows both a cleared authority cell and a recorded product filing disposition before its gate opens.

checklist.step: Release the launch gate jurisdiction by jurisdiction
actions: Release each jurisdiction only when its certificate cell, its Art. 123 position where applicable, and its product filing are all closed.
Publish the earliest permitted bind date per jurisdiction to Underwriting, Distribution and the implementation team.
Keep every unreleased jurisdiction visibly blocked on the launch plan with the outstanding item and its owner named.
Record the release decision, its date and the approver against each jurisdiction.
checklist.done: each released jurisdiction has a recorded release decision, an earliest permitted bind date and no open authority or filing item.

checklist.step: Monitor bound business against the authority matrix
actions: Run a weekly exception report of policies bound by entity, jurisdiction and statutory line against the cleared matrix.
Investigate every hit the same week, reading the policy to determine the true risk situs rather than trusting the mailing address.
Where an out-of-authority bind is confirmed, escalate to the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel the same day with the premium and policy count.
Feed each confirmed cause back into the bind-time configuration so the same gap cannot recur.
checklist.done: a weekly exception report is run and cleared, with confirmed out-of-authority binds escalated the same day and the configuration gap fixed.

checklist.step: Maintain certificates through renewal and amendment
actions: Track each certificate's renewal or continuation requirement, including annual renewal fees and any statement of continued licensure the state requires.
File corporate amendment applications when the entity name, address, officers, directors or lines change, and update the certificate image on file when the amended certificate arrives.
Notify the Regulatory Affairs Manager whenever a line is added or removed so the authority matrix and the bind-time control are updated the same week.
Record every certificate event with its date on the licence register.
checklist.done: certificates are renewed and amended on time and every line change reaches the authority matrix and the bind control within the week.

checklist.step: Remediate any writing done without authority
actions: Quantify the exposure: policies, premium, in-force count and claims paid in the affected entity, jurisdiction and line.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel and General Counsel between self-report, policy rescission or reinsurance to an authorised carrier, and record the reasoning.
Stop the writing immediately by removing the combination from the bind-time matrix before any remediation is negotiated.
Track the remediation to closure and report it to the Audit Committee, noting the Art. 315 penalty exposure where the Japan entity is affected.
checklist.done: writing is stopped at bind time, the exposure is quantified, a counsel-cleared remediation route is chosen and Audit Committee reporting is done.

checklist.step: Archive the authority evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the market entry file into the evidence repository under entity and jurisdiction: certificate images, line mapping with sources, Art. 123 determination and receipts, counsel clearance and the release decisions.
Apply the retention label of 10 years from the date the entity ceases writing the line so the record survives a later examination.
Confirm the record is searchable by entity, jurisdiction, statutory line and first-bind date.
Close the market entry tasks only after the archive is confirmed.
checklist.done: the market entry file is archived by entity and jurisdiction, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by statutory line.

testing.step: Build the population of bound business by entity, jurisdiction and line
actions: Extract every policy bound in the period with the writing entity, the risk situs jurisdiction, the statutory line, the bind date and the written premium.
Derive the situs from the insured property or resident address on the policy rather than the billing address.
Reconcile the extract premium total to the direct written premium in the period reporting so no book of business is missing.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date, record count and premium total.
testing.done: the bound-business population is situs-derived, reconciled to direct written premium and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the certificate register
actions: Extract the certificate register with entity, jurisdiction, statutory lines and effective and expiry dates.
Match each population row to a certificate covering that entity, jurisdiction and line, with the certificate effective before the bind date.
List every unmatched row with its premium and policy count as a potential unlicensed-writing exception.
Confirm the certificate register itself matches the certificate images held by the Corporate Secretary for the jurisdictions with unmatched rows.
testing.done: every bound policy matches a certificate effective before its bind date, or is listed as a potential unlicensed-writing exception with premium quantified.

testing.step: Draw and document the authority sample
actions: Take 100 percent of market entries released in the period and 100 percent of unmatched population rows.
Take 30 entity, jurisdiction and line combinations at random with a recorded seed from the matched population, weighted to newly released jurisdictions.
Record the population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every combination whose certificate was amended during the period as a mandatory sample item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all releases, all unmatched rows, 30 random combinations and every amended certificate is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the certificate coverage read on the sample
actions: Open the certificate image for each sampled combination and read the line schedule yourself before looking at the matrix cell.
Reach your own conclusion on whether the line written is named on the certificate, then compare to the recorded determination.
Treat right answer with the wrong certificate page attached as an exception, since the evidence would fail an examiner.
Where the certificate is more than 12 months old, confirm a current status letter or certificate of compliance supports it.
testing.done: each sampled combination carries an independent coverage conclusion compared to the recorded determination, with evidence pages verified.

testing.step: Verify the statutory line mapping against the jurisdiction source
actions: For each sampled combination, open the jurisdiction's line-of-authority list or the ordinance business category list and re-map the product independently.
Compare your mapping to the recorded mapping and flag differences, particularly products that legitimately span two lines.
Check the mapping source citation on the record is the current edition and note the read date.
Log any mapping that relied on an internal classification rather than a jurisdiction source.
testing.done: each sampled product is independently re-mapped to the jurisdiction's own line names with mapping-source citations verified as current.

testing.step: Trace every Art. 123 change to a dated approval or notification
actions: List every change put into use during the period to the statement of business procedures, the policy conditions, or the premium and reserve calculation methods.
For each, read the change-category determination and independently judge whether prior approval or notification was required under Art. 123 and the ordinance.
Obtain the FSA approval or notification receipt and compare its date to the first date the changed document was used in practice.
Treat use before approval, or a notification filed where approval was required, as a reportable statutory breach.
testing.done: every Art. 123 change has an independently judged category and a receipt dated before first use, or is reported as a breach.

testing.step: Test the bind-time control by attempted transaction
actions: In the test environment, attempt to quote and bind in three combinations absent from the authority matrix and confirm each is refused with a logged reason.
Attempt a bind in a combination present but with a future earliest permitted bind date and confirm the override requires a named approver.
Extract the override log for the period and confirm each production override has an approver and a written justification.
Log any override granted without justification as a control failure regardless of whether authority actually existed.
testing.done: the platform refuses out-of-matrix binds in test, and every production override in the period has a named approver and written justification.

testing.step: Recompute the launch gate timing against approval dates
actions: For each released market entry, compare the first actual bind date in the policy population to the certificate effective date and the Art. 123 approval date.
Compare the first bind date to the product filing approval or acceptance date recorded for that jurisdiction.
Compute the number of days between the latest gating date and the first bind, and flag any negative value as writing ahead of authority.
Confirm the release decision date on the launch plan pre-dates the first bind.
testing.done: for every release, the first bind date is proven to fall after the latest of certificate, Art. 123 and product filing dates, with any negative gap flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the entity, jurisdiction, statutory line, policy count, premium and the date range affected.
Assign a root cause from the standard set: line mapping error, stale certificate, matrix not updated after amendment, override abuse, or Art. 123 category error.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and open a self-report assessment with General Counsel for every confirmed unlicensed-writing or use-before-approval case.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's authority test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has a tracked issue quantifying premium and policy count, a root cause, an owner and a self-report assessment where statutory.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the authority test
actions: Compute the count and premium of policies bound outside authority and the count of Art. 123 changes used before approval, and compare both to the zero thresholds.
Write the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper reference behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who made and approved no sampled determination, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and every unlicensed-writing case to the Compliance Committee and the General Counsel, and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating out-of-authority premium, the conclusion and the committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Producer Compliance Manager owns the licence-before-solicitation gate; Producer Licensing Coordinator runs the daily checks and Distribution Operations Manager owns the channel consequence of a failed check

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Insurance Business Act Art. 3 and Art. 4 (licence and licence application requirements for carrying on insurance business) with Art. 315 (criminal sanction for unlicensed business), read alongside the Act's registration requirement for insurance solicitors; US producer licensing verified against each state's producer licensing statute and the NAIC state licensing handbook entry

In-scope processes.value: Producer onboarding and ongoing eligibility: pre-solicitation licence verification, pre-appointment eligibility verification, continuing education and renewal monitoring, and the block on quoting or submitting business by an unlicensed or lapsed producer

In-scope systems.value: Producer Database lookups and licence transactions through the NIPR Gateway, mirrored into the producer management system that gates portal access

Compliance procedure documented.value: Producer Licence Verification Procedure - pre-solicitation PDB check, licence class and line-of-authority match, background and regulatory action review, licence application submission, renewal and CE monitoring, and the access block on lapse

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Distribution and the Head of Compliance; reviewed annually and on any state licensing law change or NIPR transaction change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous - the licence check must pass before the producer solicits and again before appointment; renewals tracked to each state's licence expiry, CE compliance tracked to each state's CE due date, and regulatory action reporting within 30 days of the action

Deadline reminders configured.value: Renewal alerts at 90, 60 and 30 days before licence expiry and CE alerts at 120 and 60 days before the CE due date, to the producer, the agency principal and the Producer Licensing Coordinator

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Dated PDB verification records, licence numbers and lines of authority, background and regulatory action screening results, and renewal confirmations, retained 7 years after the producer relationship ends

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any solicitation, quote or submitted application by an unlicensed, wrong-line or lapsed producer is logged with the producer, the state, the dates and the policy and commission amounts affected

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every unlicensed-solicitation remediation and every decision to retain business written by a lapsed producer

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every producer who solicited, quoted or submitted business in the period by state, and every producer onboarded in the period, matched to their licence status at the transaction date

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero applications taken by a producer without an active licence in that state and line at the solicitation date, zero appointments made without a pre-appointment verification, zero commissions paid on unlicensed production

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the licence-status test runs monthly against that month's production, with a full re-verification sweep of the active producer base each quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have performed any sampled licence verification or onboarded any sampled producer

Evidence location for test results.value: Producer licensing test workpaper (production population, PDB re-verification results, status-at-transaction-date analysis, commission exposure) in the compliance evidence repository under the month and quarter

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Producer roster with licence numbers, lines of authority, PDB verification dates and appointment status by state, producible to a market conduct examination or an FSA inspection within 5 business days
