checklist.step: Take in the producer onboarding request with the states and lines needed
actions: Open the onboarding request and capture the producer's legal name, National Producer Number, tax identification number, residency state and the agency they write under.
Capture the states in which the producer will solicit and the lines of authority each of those states requires for the products they will sell.
Ask the Agency Relations Manager to confirm the intended production plan so the state and line list is not under-scoped at the start.
Create the producer record with status pending verification and no portal access.
checklist.done: the producer record exists with NPN, residency, target states, required lines and the agency named, and portal access is withheld.

checklist.step: Verify licence status in the Producer Database before any solicitation
actions: In NIPR open the Producer Database inquiry and search by National Producer Number, or by name and licence number where the NPN is unknown.
For each target state read the licence class, the licence number, the issue and expiry dates, the active status and the lines of authority granted.
Confirm the lines of authority actually include the products the producer will sell, since a life-only licence will not carry an annuity or variable product.
Save the dated PDB report to the producer record as the verification evidence and record the verification date and the verifier.
checklist.done: a dated PDB report is attached showing active status, licence number, expiry and matching lines of authority for every target state.

checklist.step: Submit the licence application where a state licence is missing
actions: In the NIPR Gateway open the non-resident licence application for the state and confirm the resident state licence is active first, since non-resident licensure depends on it.
Complete the uniform application including the background questions, pay the state fee and submit, capturing the transaction confirmation number.
Track the state's processing and record the issued licence number, effective date and lines of authority on the producer record when it arrives.
Where the state requires pre-licensing education or an examination, book it and hold the record at pending until the licence is issued.
checklist.done: the application is submitted with a captured confirmation number and the producer stays at pending until the issued licence details are recorded.

checklist.step: Screen background and regulatory action history
actions: Read the regulatory actions section of the PDB report for every state, including administrative actions, suspensions, revocations and surrenders.
Run the background and criminal history screen the onboarding standard requires and review any felony or financial crime result against the eligibility policy.
For any adverse finding, obtain the producer's written explanation and the state's order, and route the file to the Head of Compliance for a documented decision.
Record the screening date, the sources checked and the eligibility decision on the producer record.
checklist.done: regulatory actions and background results are reviewed, adverse findings have a documented decision, and the screening is dated on the record.

checklist.step: Complete product and suitability training before release
actions: Assign the product training and, for annuity and variable products, the state-required annuity suitability and product-specific training modules.
Assign the anti-money laundering training and the market conduct and replacement rules training required for the lines being sold.
Record completion date and score for each module and hold the release where a state requires training completion before solicitation.
Export the training completion record to the producer file as evidence for a market conduct examination.
checklist.done: every required product, suitability and conduct module shows a completion date on the producer file before release to solicit.

checklist.step: Release solicitation authority and open portal access
actions: Move the producer record to active only when the PDB verification, the screening decision and the training records are all complete for the states being opened.
Grant portal access limited to the exact states and product lines the licence covers, not the full catalogue.
Confirm the quoting system inherits the state and line restriction so an unlicensed state cannot be selected on a quote.
Notify the Agency Relations Manager and the producer of the exact states and lines now open.
checklist.done: portal and quoting access is limited to verified states and lines and the producer is notified of the exact scope opened.

checklist.step: Verify licence again immediately before appointment
actions: Re-run the PDB inquiry on the appointment date rather than relying on the onboarding verification, since status can change between the two.
Confirm the licence is still active, the lines still cover the products, and no regulatory action has been added since the last check.
Attach the fresh PDB report to the appointment record as the pre-appointment verification evidence the state expects.
Refuse to release the appointment transaction where the licence lapsed, and return the producer record to pending.
checklist.done: a PDB report dated the appointment date is attached to the appointment record and no appointment proceeds on a lapsed licence.

checklist.step: Run the daily licence status refresh against the active roster
actions: Subscribe the active producer roster to the NIPR alert or reconciliation service so status changes flow back daily by NPN.
Load the daily file into the producer management system and update licence status, expiry dates, lines of authority and regulatory actions.
Produce an exception list of producers whose status changed to inactive, expired, suspended or revoked since the last run.
Route the exception list to the Producer Compliance Manager the same day it is produced.
checklist.done: a daily status refresh updates the roster and a same-day exception list of status downgrades reaches the Producer Compliance Manager.

checklist.step: Block access the day a licence lapses or is actioned
actions: On any exception list entry, remove quoting and submission rights for the affected state and line the same business day.
Notify the producer and the agency principal in writing of the block, the reason and what is needed to restore access.
Hold any in-flight application from that producer in that state for a compliance decision rather than issuing it.
Record the block date, the reason and the restoring event on the producer record.
checklist.done: access is removed the same business day as the status downgrade, in-flight business is held, and the block is recorded with its reason.

checklist.step: Monitor renewals and continuing education to the state due dates
actions: Maintain each producer's licence expiry date and CE due date by state from the PDB feed rather than from producer self-report.
Send renewal reminders at 90, 60 and 30 days and CE reminders at 120 and 60 days to the producer and the agency principal.
Where the company pays the renewal, submit the renewal through the NIPR Gateway before the expiry date and capture the confirmation.
Escalate any producer inside 30 days of expiry with no renewal in progress to the Agency Relations Manager for direct contact.
checklist.done: every active producer has a tracked expiry and CE date with reminders sent, and inside-30-day cases are escalated for direct contact.

checklist.step: Report regulatory actions and licence changes as the states require
actions: On learning of an administrative action against a producer, record the state, the order date, the conduct and the sanction.
Report the action to the states that require notification within their reporting window, commonly 30 days from the action.
Assess whether the action affects the producer's eligibility to continue representing the company and record the decision with the Head of Compliance.
Attach the order and the notification receipts to the producer file.
checklist.done: every known regulatory action is recorded, reported inside the state window, and carries an eligibility decision with the order on file.

checklist.step: Reconcile the producer roster to actual production monthly
actions: Extract every application and policy in the month with the writing producer NPN, the state, the line and the application signature date.
Match each to the producer's licence status on the application signature date, not on today's date.
List every transaction where the producer had no active licence for that state and line on that date, with premium and commission.
Send the list to the Producer Compliance Manager and the Head of Compliance the same week it is produced.
checklist.done: monthly production is matched to licence status as at the signature date and every unlicensed transaction is listed with premium and commission.

checklist.step: Hold commission on production that fails the licence check
actions: Suspend commission payment on every transaction on the unlicensed production list before the next commission cycle runs.
Where commission has already paid, raise the chargeback and record the amount, the producer and the cycle it will be recovered in.
Release the hold only on written confirmation from the Producer Compliance Manager that the licence was in fact active at the signature date.
Report held and charged-back amounts to the Head of Distribution monthly.
checklist.done: commission is suspended or charged back on every unlicensed transaction and released only on written compliance confirmation.

checklist.step: Remediate unlicensed solicitation to a decided outcome
actions: Quantify the exposure: policies, premium, in-force count, commission paid and the states affected.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel between self-report to the state, reassignment of the business to a licensed producer of record, or rescission, and record the reasoning.
Confirm the producer's access remains blocked until the licence is genuinely issued and verified in the PDB.
Report the case and the Art. 315 exposure where the Japan entity is affected to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: the exposure is quantified, a counsel-cleared outcome is chosen and recorded, access stays blocked and the case is reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Archive the producer licensing evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the producer file into the evidence repository: PDB verification reports with dates, licence and application confirmations, screening results, training completions and renewal confirmations.
Apply the retention label of 7 years after the producer relationship ends so the record survives a market conduct examination lookback.
Confirm the record is searchable by NPN, producer name, state and licence number.
Close the onboarding or termination tasks only after the archive is confirmed.
checklist.done: the producer file is archived with dated verification evidence, labelled for 7-year post-relationship retention and searchable by NPN.

testing.step: Build the population of producers who produced business in the period
actions: Extract every application and policy in the period with the writing producer NPN, the state, the line, the application signature date and the premium.
Add quotes and illustrations produced in the portal so solicitation without a subsequent sale is captured, since solicitation is the trigger, not the sale.
Reconcile the transaction count to the production reporting for the period and resolve any difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date, record count and premium total.
testing.done: the population covers quotes as well as applications, reconciles to production reporting, and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the active producer roster
actions: Extract the producer roster with NPN, state, licence number, status, lines of authority and effective and expiry dates as held internally.
Match each transaction to a roster record on NPN and state and list every transaction with no roster record.
List every roster record with production but no verification evidence attached.
Confirm the roster count agrees with the count of producers holding open portal access.
testing.done: every transaction matches a roster record with verification evidence, and roster-to-portal-access counts agree.

testing.step: Draw and document the producer sample
actions: Take 100 percent of producers onboarded in the period and 100 percent of producers appearing on any unlicensed production list.
Take 40 producers at random with a recorded seed from the remaining producing population, spread across states and agencies.
Record the population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample is reproducible.
Add every producer whose status changed during the period as a mandatory sample item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all new and flagged producers, 40 random producers and every status change is documented.

testing.step: Re-verify each sampled producer directly in the Producer Database
actions: Run your own PDB inquiry by NPN for each sampled producer and read licence class, number, status, expiry, lines of authority and regulatory actions.
Compare each field to the internal roster record and to the verification report on file, and log any field that differs.
Confirm the lines of authority genuinely cover the products the producer sold, rather than covering the general line only.
Capture the PDB screen into the workpaper as the independent evidence.
testing.done: each sampled producer is independently re-verified in the PDB with every differing field logged and the screen captured.

testing.step: Test licence status as at each transaction date
actions: For each sampled producer's transactions, compare the application signature date or quote date to the licence effective and expiry dates for that state.
Flag any transaction dated before the licence effective date or after the expiry date, and any transaction in a line the licence does not carry.
Recompute the gap in days between the transaction date and the licence date so the size of the exposure is measurable.
Treat a transaction inside a lapse and reinstatement gap as an exception even where the licence was later reinstated retroactively.
testing.done: every sampled transaction has its date compared to the licence period and line, with day gaps computed for each exception.

testing.step: Test pre-appointment verification evidence
actions: For each sampled appointment, confirm a PDB verification report exists dated on or immediately before the appointment date.
Confirm the report shows an active licence in that state with the lines the appointment covers.
Log any appointment whose only verification is the onboarding check taken weeks or months earlier.
Confirm no appointment exists for a producer whose licence was inactive on the appointment date.
testing.done: each sampled appointment carries a contemporaneous PDB verification showing an active licence and matching lines.

testing.step: Test the access block and the daily status refresh
actions: Take every status downgrade in the period from the NIPR exception lists and find the corresponding portal access removal date.
Compute the number of business days between the downgrade and the access removal and flag anything over one business day.
Attempt a test quote in the portal as a producer flagged inactive and confirm the system refuses the state and line.
Confirm in-flight applications from downgraded producers were held rather than issued.
testing.done: access removal is proven within one business day of every downgrade, the portal refuses an inactive test producer, and in-flight business was held.

testing.step: Trace commission held or recovered on unlicensed production
actions: For each transaction identified as unlicensed, extract the commission calculated, paid and recovered from the commission platform.
Confirm a hold or chargeback exists for every such transaction and quantify any commission still paid out.
Confirm every released hold has the written Producer Compliance Manager confirmation behind it and that the confirmation cites a verified licence date.
Total the commission exposure by state and by agency for the exception report.
testing.done: commission on every unlicensed transaction is traced to a hold or chargeback, with releases evidenced and total exposure quantified by state.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the producer, NPN, state, line, transaction dates, policy count, premium and commission.
Assign a root cause from the standard set: verification skipped, stale verification, wrong line of authority, status refresh gap, access block delay, or renewal missed.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel for confirmed unlicensed solicitation.
Carry every open exception into the next month's producer test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has a tracked issue quantifying premium and commission, a root cause, an owner and a self-report assessment where confirmed.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the producer licensing test
actions: Compute the unlicensed transaction count, the affected premium and commission, and the pre-appointment verification rate against the zero thresholds.
Write the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper reference behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed no sampled verification and onboarded no sampled producer, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and every unlicensed-solicitation case to the Compliance Committee and the Head of Distribution, and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating unlicensed counts, affected premium, the conclusion and the committee reporting date is in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Producer Licensing Coordinator processes every appointment and termination transaction; Producer Compliance Manager owns the statutory windows and the for-cause reporting decision

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Insurance Business Act Art. 115, Art. 116 and Art. 117 as the reserve provisions that make producer-generated in-force accurate, read with the Act's solicitor registration and notification requirements; each US state's appointment and termination window verified against its producer licensing statute and the NAIC state licensing handbook entry

In-scope processes.value: Event-driven appointment and termination processing: appointment submission within the state window from the first application or contract date, termination notice to the state within its window, notice to the producer, for-cause reporting, and the resulting change to producer-of-record and commission rights

In-scope systems.value: Appointment and termination transactions submitted through the NIPR Gateway and reconciled back into the producer management system that drives commission and portal rights

Compliance procedure documented.value: Appointment and Termination Processing Procedure - trigger definition, per-state window table, submission and confirmation capture, producer notice, for-cause determination and reporting, and the downstream access and commission consequences

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Distribution and the Head of Compliance; the per-state window table is reverified annually against each state's statute and on any licensing law change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven - appointment filed within the state's window from the first application or the contract date, commonly 15 days; termination notice to the state within the state window, commonly 30 days from the effective date; notice to the producer commonly within 15 days of notifying the state

Deadline reminders configured.value: Each appointment or termination event creates a task dated at the state window minus 5 days, escalating daily to the Producer Compliance Manager once inside 3 days of the statutory limit

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Appointment and termination confirmations from the state, the trigger evidence with its date, the producer notice with proof of delivery and the for-cause file, retained 7 years after the producer relationship ends

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Appointments filed after the state window, terminations reported late or not at all, producer notices not sent, and for-cause terminations reported as voluntary are logged with the state, producer and days late

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Producer Compliance Manager signs off every late appointment or termination remediation and every for-cause reporting decision

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every appointment and every termination event in the period by producer and state, including terminations arising from non-renewal, contract cancellation and for-cause events

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero appointments filed after the state window, zero terminations reported after the state window, zero missing producer notices, zero for-cause events reported as voluntary

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; testing runs monthly across that month's events, with a full annual reconciliation of the state appointment registry to the internal roster

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have processed any sampled appointment or termination transaction

Evidence location for test results.value: Appointment and termination timeliness workpaper (event population, window recomputation, confirmation tracing, registry reconciliation) in the compliance evidence repository under the month

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-state appointment and termination registers with trigger dates, submission dates, confirmations and producer notices, producible to a market conduct examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance Manager answers state inquiries on appointment and termination records; General Counsel clears any for-cause reporting content given the defamation and immunity considerations

checklist.step: Maintain the per-state appointment and termination window table
actions: For each state record the appointment trigger the statute uses - first application submitted, or the agency contract date - and the number of days allowed to file.
Record the termination notice window to the state and the separate window for the notice to the producer, and whether the state requires a reason code.
Record whether the state permits appointment by the insurer only or requires the agency appointment as well, and the fee for each transaction.
Cite the statute section and the date read on every row and reverify the whole table annually.
checklist.done: every state row shows the trigger, both windows, the reason-code requirement and the fee, with a cited statute and read date.

checklist.step: Detect appointment triggers the day they occur
actions: Run a daily feed of first applications submitted by producer and state from policy administration and of newly executed agency contracts from the contract record.
For each trigger, create an appointment task with the trigger date, the state, the producer NPN and the computed statutory due date from the window table.
Confirm the producer holds an active licence in that state and line before the appointment is submitted, using the current PDB record.
Escalate any trigger where the producer is unlicensed to the Producer Compliance Manager immediately rather than appointing regardless.
checklist.done: every appointment trigger generates a dated task with a computed statutory due date and a licence check completed before submission.

checklist.step: Submit the appointment through the NIPR Gateway
actions: In the NIPR Gateway open the appointment transaction, select the state, the appointing company by NAIC company code and the producer by NPN.
Select the lines of authority the appointment covers, matching them to the licence lines and to the products the producer will sell.
Submit with the state fee and capture the transaction confirmation number and the submission timestamp.
Record the confirmation on the appointment task and leave the task open until the state returns the effective date.
checklist.done: the appointment is submitted with matched lines and fee, and the confirmation number and timestamp are recorded on the task.

checklist.step: Confirm the state accepted the appointment and record its effective date
actions: Monitor the NIPR transaction status until the state returns accepted, and read the appointment effective date the state assigned.
Where the transaction is rejected, read the reason - unlicensed producer, wrong line, fee failure, duplicate - correct it and resubmit inside the remaining window.
Update the producer record with the appointment effective date, the state and the lines so commission and portal rights key off the confirmed data.
Close the task only on an accepted status with an effective date, never on submission alone.
checklist.done: every appointment task closes on an accepted state status with a recorded effective date, and rejections are corrected inside the window.

checklist.step: Reconcile appointments to production monthly
actions: Extract every policy issued in the month with the writing producer, the state and the issue date.
Match each to an accepted appointment for that producer, company and state effective on or before the required date under the state's rule.
List every policy with no matching appointment as an exception with the producer, state, policy count and premium.
Send the list to the Producer Compliance Manager the same week and hold commission on the affected policies.
checklist.done: every issued policy matches an accepted appointment or is listed as an exception with commission held.

checklist.step: Detect termination triggers and classify the reason
actions: Capture every termination trigger the day it is decided: contract cancellation by either side, non-renewal, retirement, death, agency dissolution or a for-cause decision.
Record the termination effective date and the reason, and map the reason to the state's required reason code where the state uses one.
Where the reason involves misconduct - fraud, misappropriation, forgery, misrepresentation, unlicensed activity - flag it for the for-cause path rather than recording it as voluntary.
Notify the Producer Licensing Coordinator the same day so the state notice window starts running from a recorded date.
checklist.done: every termination has a recorded effective date, a mapped reason code and a for-cause flag where misconduct is involved, notified same day.

checklist.step: Run the for-cause determination with Legal before reporting
actions: Assemble the evidence behind the misconduct allegation: the investigation file, the customer complaints, the transaction records and the producer's response.
Review with Legal Counsel whether the facts meet the state's for-cause reporting standard, and record the conclusion and the reasoning.
Draft the reporting narrative to state facts and findings without characterisation beyond what the evidence supports.
Obtain Legal Counsel written clearance of the narrative before it is submitted to any state.
checklist.done: the for-cause determination is evidenced, tested against the state standard and its narrative is cleared in writing by Legal before submission.

checklist.step: Report the termination to every state inside its window
actions: In the NIPR Gateway open the termination transaction and submit for every state where the producer is appointed with that company, using the recorded effective date and reason code.
Compute each state's due date as the effective date plus the state's window, commonly 30 days, and submit before it.
Attach the cleared for-cause narrative where the state requires the additional statement with the termination.
Capture the confirmation number and the accepted status for each state on the termination record.
checklist.done: a termination is submitted and accepted for every appointed state before its computed due date, with the for-cause statement attached where required.

checklist.step: Send the producer notice inside its own window
actions: Prepare the written notice to the producer stating the termination, its effective date and the fact that the state has been notified, using the template cleared by Legal.
Send it within the state's producer notice window, commonly 15 days from the state notification, by a method that produces proof of delivery.
Where the state requires a copy of the exact statement filed with the state, include it rather than a summary.
File the notice and the delivery proof on the producer record with the send date.
checklist.done: the producer notice is sent inside the state window with proof of delivery filed and the send date recorded.

checklist.step: Cut off access and commission rights on the effective date
actions: Remove quoting, submission and policy-servicing access for the terminated producer on the termination effective date, not on the processing date.
Set the commission treatment per the contract: stop new business commission, and set renewal commission to vest or to cease per the contract terms and the reason.
Reassign the producer of record on in-force policies to a licensed and appointed producer or to a house account, and record the reassignment date.
Notify affected policyholders where the reassignment changes their servicing contact.
checklist.done: access ends on the effective date, commission treatment follows the contract and reason, and every in-force policy has a new servicing owner recorded.

checklist.step: Track and clear rejected termination transactions
actions: Monitor the NIPR status list daily for rejected termination transactions and read the rejection reason on each.
Correct the reason code, the effective date or the company selection and resubmit inside the remaining statutory window.
Where the window has already closed, log the late report immediately and prepare the explanation the state expects.
Confirm no producer remains appointed in the state registry after the termination is accepted.
checklist.done: no termination remains in rejected status and the state registry shows no live appointment for any terminated producer.

checklist.step: Reconcile the state appointment registry to the internal roster
actions: Pull the appointment listing by company and state from the Producer Database and compare it to the internal appointed-producer roster.
Investigate producers appointed in the state registry but terminated internally, since these carry ongoing appointment fees and examination risk.
Investigate producers active internally but not appointed in the registry, since these are unappointed production waiting to be found.
Clear every difference with a submitted transaction or a corrected internal record and record the clearance date.
checklist.done: the state registry and the internal roster agree producer by producer and state by state, with every difference cleared and dated.

checklist.step: Manage appointment renewals and fee cycles
actions: Track each state's appointment renewal cycle and the invoice date, since a missed renewal terminates the appointment by operation of law in some states.
Review the renewal list against the internal roster and drop producers who are terminated or no longer producing before paying the fee.
Submit the renewal and pay the fee before the state's cut-off and capture the confirmation.
Reconcile the fee invoice to the renewed appointment count and query any difference with the state.
checklist.done: appointment renewals are submitted and paid before each state cut-off with the invoice reconciled to the renewed appointment count.

checklist.step: Report timeliness and open exceptions to Distribution leadership
actions: Build a monthly report showing appointments and terminations processed, on-time rate against the state windows, and the count of late transactions by state.
Show unappointed production and the registry reconciliation differences outstanding at month end.
Circulate to the Head of Distribution, the Head of Compliance and the Distribution Operations Manager within 5 business days of month end.
Present every late transaction with the producer, state, days late, cause and the named remediation owner.
checklist.done: a monthly on-time and exception report reaches Distribution and Compliance leadership within 5 business days of month end.

checklist.step: Archive the appointment and termination evidence
actions: Move each event file into the evidence repository: trigger evidence with its date, NIPR confirmations, state acceptance, producer notice with delivery proof and the for-cause file where applicable.
Apply the retention label of 7 years after the producer relationship ends.
Confirm the record is searchable by NPN, state, event type and effective date so a single event can be produced on examination request.
Close the event tasks only after the archive is confirmed.
checklist.done: each appointment and termination event is archived with confirmations and notices, labelled for 7-year retention and searchable by NPN and state.

testing.step: Build the population of appointment and termination events
actions: Extract every appointment and termination event in the period with producer NPN, state, event type, trigger date, effective date and processing date.
Independently derive appointment triggers from first-application data in policy administration and from executed agency contracts, so events never raised as tasks are captured.
Independently derive termination triggers from contract cancellations, agency dissolutions and completed misconduct investigations.
Sign the population as complete with the source systems, extract date and record count.
testing.done: the population combines logged events with independently derived triggers and is signed as complete with sources named.

testing.step: Reconcile the internal roster to the state appointment registry
actions: Pull the company's appointment listing by state from the Producer Database on the test date.
Compare it producer by producer to the internal appointed roster and quantify appointed-not-internal and internal-not-appointed differences.
For each difference, determine whether a transaction was never submitted, was rejected, or was submitted and not reflected internally.
Treat every internal-not-appointed producer with production in the period as an automatic exception.
testing.done: registry and roster differences are quantified and classified, with producing unappointed producers logged as automatic exceptions.

testing.step: Draw and document the event sample
actions: Take 100 percent of for-cause terminations and 100 percent of events flagged late by the internal report.
Take 40 events at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population, split between appointments and terminations and spread across states.
Record the population size, seed, selection date and selector so the sample is reproducible.
Add every rejected and resubmitted transaction as a mandatory sample item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all for-cause and late events, 40 random events and every rejection is documented.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory window on each sampled event
actions: Read the state statute for each sampled event and independently determine the trigger and the number of days allowed.
Recompute the due date from the trigger date and compare it to the due date the internal window table produced, logging any permissive table row.
Compare the state acceptance timestamp to the recomputed due date and compute days early or late for every event.
Confirm the day count basis used matches the statute, calendar or business days, rather than an internal assumption.
testing.done: each sampled event has an independently recomputed due date from the statute and a measured days early or late figure.

testing.step: Trace each sampled event to a state confirmation
actions: Open the NIPR transaction history for each sampled producer and locate the appointment or termination transaction by state and date.
Confirm accepted status, the company NAIC code, the state, the lines and the effective date the state assigned.
Compare the state effective date to the internal record and log any difference, since commission and access rights key off it.
Treat an event whose only evidence is an internal status flag as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled event is confirmed accepted in the NIPR transaction history with the state effective date agreed to the internal record.

testing.step: Test the for-cause classification and reporting content
actions: Read the investigation file behind each sampled termination classified as voluntary and judge independently whether the facts met the state's for-cause standard.
For each for-cause event, confirm the narrative filed with the state matches the cleared version and states facts rather than conclusions.
Confirm a written Legal clearance pre-dates the filing and that the required additional statement was filed where the state demands it.
Treat any misconduct termination reported as voluntary as a reportable exception, not a classification preference.
testing.done: every sampled termination has an independently judged classification and every for-cause filing matches a pre-dated Legal clearance.

testing.step: Test producer notice delivery and timing
actions: For each sampled termination, locate the producer notice and its proof of delivery on the producer record.
Compute the days between the state notification date and the notice send date and compare to the state's producer notice window.
Confirm the notice content matches what the state requires, including a copy of the filed statement where that is prescribed.
Log any termination with no notice, no delivery proof, or a notice sent outside the window.
testing.done: every sampled termination has a delivered producer notice inside the state window with content matching the state requirement.

testing.step: Test the downstream access and commission cut-off
actions: For each sampled termination, extract portal access removal dates and compare them to the termination effective date.
Extract commission paid after the effective date and confirm each payment is permitted by the contract vesting terms for that termination reason.
Confirm the producer of record was reassigned on the in-force book and that no policy remains assigned to a terminated producer.
Quantify any commission paid contrary to the contract and any policy still assigned to a terminated producer.
testing.done: access removal, commission treatment and producer-of-record reassignment are proven against the effective date, with any breach quantified.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the producer, NPN, state, event type, trigger date, due date, actual date and days late.
Assign a root cause from the standard set: trigger not detected, window table error, rejection not reworked, notice not sent, misclassified for-cause, or registry not reconciled.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and file the late transaction with the state immediately with the explanation it expects.
Carry every open exception into the next month's event test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has a tracked issue with days late, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and an immediate late filing where applicable.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the appointment and termination test
actions: Compute the on-time rate for appointments and for terminations, the producer notice rate and the registry reconciliation difference count against the zero thresholds.
Write the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, citing the workpaper reference behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who processed no sampled transaction, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, late state notifications and any misclassified for-cause event to the Compliance Committee and the Head of Distribution, and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating on-time rates, notice rates, the conclusion and the committee reporting date is in the evidence repository.
